It raised a $6.8M seed round in August 2023 led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with Initialized Capital. The original domain braid.ai is now a domain-for-sale listing at atom.com and braid.social no longer resolves. The same legal entity now ships "Braid Teams" at trybraid.io (mirrored at braidsocial.com) — an AI-powered employee-engagement copilot that runs inside Slack, automating icebreakers, games, polls, events, reminders, leaderboards, and engagement reporting for distributed teams, on a free / $5-per-user Premium / contact-us Enterprise plan. Braid Teams is a Slack-app product with no public developer program: no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI, no SDKs, and no GitHub organization. The only machine surface is the private application backend at core.trybraid.io, which answers {"status":"ok"} at its root and 404s every spec, docs and /.well-known/ path. The homepage states the product is "Currently not accepting new users" and the Slack install endpoint returns HTTP 500.

providers.name: 8Tracks
providers.description: 8tracks was a San Francisco-based internet radio and social music-streaming service that let people create and share handcrafted playlists ("mixes") of at least eight tracks, discover mixes by mood, activity, genre, and tag, and play them back through the web, iOS, and Android apps. Founded in 2008, it grew to more than eight million monthly listeners by 2014 before declining. 8tracks published a public REST API (v2/v3) that exposed mix discovery, playback token sessions, track skip/report events, and user likes/favorites, but stopped issuing new API keys in February 2015. The company ceased operations on December 31, 2019, briefly relaunched under BackBeat Inc. in April 2020, and the service has been inactive since. This profile documents the historical API surface and web properties.

providers.name: ChannelMeter
providers.description: ChannelMeter is a creator management and payments platform for multi-channel networks, agencies, and brands. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Francisco, it provides an all-in-one suite for creator discovery, onboarding, contract management, analytics, and automated global payouts. Its Creator Pay product moves money to creators across 21+ currencies and 50+ countries, and Creator Cash offers cash advances to creators. ChannelMeter reports having processed over $1B in payments to more than one million creators, working with Stripe and Fifth Third Bank for financial services. The company is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Horizon Media
providers.description: Horizon Media is the largest independent media agency in the United States, founded in 1989 by Bill Koenigsberg and headquartered at 75 Varick Street in New York with offices in Los Angeles and Toronto. The agency employs roughly 2,300+ people, is ranked the third largest US media agency by COMvergence, and manages an estimated $8.7 billion in billings. Horizon operates a portfolio of specialty units (Horizon Next for performance, Blue Hour Studios for social/creator, Night Market for retail media, Scout Sports for sponsorship via Horizon Sports & Experiences, and the WHY Group for cultural insights) and runs a proprietary data and AI stack anchored by the Blu platform. In 2025 Horizon formed Horizon Global, a 50/50 US joint venture with Havas positioned at roughly $20 billion in combined billings, merging Blu with Havas Converged into a shared platform branded BluConverged, and is also building Horizon OS (Open Sphere) as an orchestration layer over the programmatic ad-tech stack. In June 2026 Horizon launched an agentic integration layer around Blu — a set of Blu audience APIs, MCP endpoints and agent-based integration points that ad-tech, media-owner and martech partners can build on — but that surface is partner-gated: Horizon publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no SDKs in any public registry, and its GitHub organization has zero public repositories. The only route to the API is the corporate contact form. All platforms documented here are proprietary systems reachable through a commercial partnership rather than open developer APIs.

providers.name: 24Symbols
providers.description: 24Symbols is a digital reading subscription service, often described as a "Spotify for books," giving readers unlimited access to a catalog of more than 500,000 e-books across Spanish, English, German, Italian, Portuguese, and French for a flat monthly fee. Founded in Madrid and backed by Seedcamp, the platform lets subscribers read on smartphones, tablets, e-readers, and the web, build personal bookshelves, track reading progress, and follow other readers and authors through its social reading community. Alongside its consumer premium plan, 24Symbols offers B2B "reading space" solutions that let hotels, telecoms, media outlets, educational institutions, and loyalty or employee programs license library access for their audiences. The company operates as a consumer- and business-facing subscription product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration surface; this profile captures its verifiable identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Audiodraft
providers.description: Audiodraft is a Helsinki-founded global audio branding and custom music production company that helps brands design, create, and manage their sonic identity across advertising, video, games, and campaigns. Its service is organized around three offerings — ANALYZE (data-driven audio strategy and brand-attribute analysis), CREATE (custom music, sound design, and voice-over production), and MANAGE (brand-fit validation and sound testing) — drawing on a crowdsourced community of thousands of composers and sound designers across 100+ countries. Audiodraft has worked with brands and agencies including Nokia, Red Bull Media House, Finnair, Fortum, and TBWA. It is a creative audio-branding services provider and does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Blockpartyapp
providers.description: Block Party is a consumer privacy tool — a browser extension (Chrome, Firefox, and Edge) that helps people deep-clean and secure their social media presence. It scans connected accounts for privacy and security exposures, then automates bulk cleanup across Facebook, X/Twitter, Instagram, Reddit, and LinkedIn: deleting old posts, likes, and comments, untagging photos, removing connections, stripping location data, and tightening privacy settings. Founded by Tracy Chou, Block Party (also branded Privacy Party) is a consumer-facing application and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Botika
providers.description: Botika is an AI fashion-photography platform that helps online clothing and e-commerce brands replace traditional model photoshoots with generative AI. It turns flat-lay, mannequin, and basic on-model product photos into studio-quality images featuring fully AI-generated fashion models, poses, and on-brand backgrounds. Founded by Eran Dagan and Yarin Didi Meir and backed by an $8M seed round with participation from Seedcamp, Botika ships a web console, a native Shopify app, and an iOS app, cutting photoshoot costs by up to 90% and speeding time-to-market roughly 3x. A public API is on the company roadmap but is not yet released, so this profile currently captures company identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Home From College
providers.description: Home From College (H\FC) is an AI-powered growth platform that connects college students with paid work from consumer brands. Students earn money and build professional experience through microGIGs (quick paid tasks such as app installs, surveys, product feedback, and social sharing with instant payment) and GIGs (larger, ongoing opportunities including content creation, brand-ambassador roles, product testing, and internships), while brands reach and activate Gen Z talent for marketing campaigns. Backed by GV, Home From College runs a two-sided marketplace across a student mobile app and a brand-facing web platform. No public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Melodics
providers.description: Melodics is a New Zealand-based interactive music-learning application that teaches drums, MIDI keyboards, and pad controllers (finger drumming) through gamified, real-time lessons. It connects to electronic instruments and MIDI controllers to give immediate feedback on timing and accuracy, offering guided learning paths, song tutorials, and structured daily practice for beginner through advanced players across desktop and mobile. Melodics is a consumer edtech product and a portfolio company of 500 Global; it publishes no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: OpenSponsorship
providers.description: OpenSponsorship is a two-sided sports sponsorship and influencer marketing marketplace that connects brands with a network of more than 25,000 professional athletes, teams, sports creators, and health and wellness influencers across 150+ sports. Brands pay a monthly subscription to search the roster, post campaigns, submit proposals, manage contracts, and track ROI, while athletes and their agents join for free with OpenSponsorship taking a commission on secured deals. The platform layers AI-based matching, social-content search, campaign management, and reporting on top of a managed service that handles matching, outreach, contracts, and reporting. OpenSponsorship exposes no public developer API at this time; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: RedCircle
providers.description: RedCircle is a podcast advertising, hosting, and monetization platform founded in 2018 that turns podcast host-read endorsements into measurable results for brands and creators. For podcasters it provides podcast hosting, RSS distribution to directories, dynamic ad insertion, a cross-promotions marketplace, instant payouts, automated transcript and video generation, and audience analytics. For brands it operates a fully managed host-read ad platform that pairs proprietary data with authentic creator voices to run and measure campaigns at scale. RedCircle also documents OpenRAP, its remote ad-pipeline / VAST configuration for dynamic ad insertion. The platform is offered as SaaS tiers (Growth, Pro, and Enterprise) rather than as a public developer API; there is no published developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK.

providers.name: Smore
providers.description: Smore is a newsletter and flyer builder purpose-built for educators, schools, and districts, letting teachers and administrators create accessible, mobile-friendly digital newsletters from customizable templates to keep families and staff informed. The product emphasizes WCAG AA accessibility, translation for multilingual families, and engagement analytics on opens and clicks. Smore is now part of SchoolStatus, the family-engagement platform. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Smore publishes no public developer program, API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface — this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed domain security posture only.

providers.name: Venue
providers.description: Venue is an all-in-one internal communications platform that makes it easy for teams to host, organize, and share all hands, webinars, AMAs, and fireside chats. It combines HD live streaming, recording, automatic transcription and summarization, branded Q&A, engagement tracking, and Channels for centralizing events and videos. Aimed at internal comms and employer-brand teams at companies like Shopify, PwC, Wealthsimple, and Yelp, Venue is a Toronto-based, Accel- and Y Combinator-backed productivity company. As of this enrichment pass Venue publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface — this profile captures its identity, website properties, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Kickstarter
providers.description: Kickstarter is a public-benefit crowdfunding platform where creators launch funding campaigns for creative projects — film, music, art, design, games, technology, publishing, and more — and backers pledge money to help bring them to life on an all-or-nothing funding model. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Brooklyn, New York, it has channeled billions of dollars in pledges to hundreds of thousands of successfully funded projects. Kickstarter does not currently operate a public developer API program or developer portal; its GraphQL and REST endpoints power its own web and mobile clients and are not documented for third-party integration. The company does maintain an active open-source GitHub organization (including its iOS and Android app source), a help center, and a company blog. This API Evangelist profile tracks Kickstarter's public developer, security, and platform surface for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Teespring
providers.description: Teespring is a creator-commerce and print-on-demand platform, founded in 2011, that lets creators design, launch, and sell custom apparel and merchandise with no upfront cost or inventory, handling production, payment, and fulfillment on the creator's behalf. Backed by a16z, the company rebranded to "Spring" in 2021 and now operates as Amaze Commerce (part of Amaze Holdings): its consumer storefront lives at spri.ng while the creator/merchant SaaS platform runs at amazecommerce.com and amaze.co. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, /.well-known discovery surface, or llms.txt; this profile therefore captures verified company identity and published site properties only.

providers.name: Wave AI
providers.description: Wave AI (WaveAI) is a Sunnyvale, California AI music company founded in 2017 by David Loker, Dr. Maya Ackerman, and Chris Cassion, building foundational generative AI models for music and songwriting. Its flagship product LyricStudio is an AI-powered lyric-writing assistant used by millions of artists and creators to generate genre- and topic-aware lyrical suggestions, rhymes, and full songs, and MelodyStudio adds generative vocal-melody and chord generation. The company is backed by 500 Global, Horizon 3 Venture Capital, Kilowatt Capital, and angel investors. Wave AI ships consumer web applications rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity and public web properties. Added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with a domain-security probe and verified public link properties.

providers.name: Dreamforge
providers.description: DreamForge.ai is an AI-powered game creation platform for building, iterating on, and publishing 2D and stylized 3D games directly in the browser. Creators use AI to generate gameplay systems, game-ready art and textures, animation, and playable web builds, then share public play pages under dreamforge.ai/play. The platform pairs a creator-facing web studio (including an Asset Studio) with a consumer application distributed on Steam, iOS, and Android. Founded in 2025 and based in Miami, Florida, DreamForge is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). DreamForge supports stylized 3D world generation, textures, voxels, and billboarding workflows; native 3D model generation is not currently provided. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published at this time.

providers.name: Twisty
providers.description: Twisty, operated by Bright Live Inc. (dba Twisty) of Santa Monica, California, is an AI character creation platform that lets creators generate lifelike AI characters and produce personalized, expressive video messages as an alternative to generic talking-head videos. The product ships as a web app plus iOS and Android apps with a free tier and a paid monthly plan, and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Twisty does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Promolta
providers.description: Promolta is a self-service video advertising platform that promotes YouTube and other videos across a network of blogs, websites, mobile apps, and social networks to grow views, subscribers, and engagement. Advertisers fund campaigns and target audiences, while publishers in the Promolta network earn by distributing sponsored video content. Promolta is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Campaigns start at a $10 minimum budget, go live within 24 hours, and can be optimized for views, YouTube likes, YouTube subscribers, or mobile app installs, with targeting by age, gender, location, and keyword. As of the 2026-08-12 enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/GraphQL contract, developer portal, or webhook surface — this profile captures its public web, legal, blog, and domain-security footprint.

providers.name: Noodle
providers.description: Noodle is a Brazilian fintech building financial infrastructure for the creator economy. It provides automated payouts to creators, influencers, and vendors; FastPay early access to future earnings; noodleOS, a unified platform for campaigns, creator data, payments, and asset tracking; global payouts powered by Ebanx; foreign-exchange settlement; and credit and capital products underwritten in part on a creator's social presence. Backed by QED Investors, Noodle serves media companies, agencies, and platforms that pay content creators. The company references API-based integrations but publishes no public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Tone
providers.description: Tone is a full-stack royalty management platform for music rights owners — independent labels, distributors, and royalty teams. It centralizes royalty accounting, income tracking, and contract management, then pays artists directly through integrated global payouts. The platform processes large royalty periods quickly, provides near-real-time sales intelligence with timeline views and customizable charts, models deal structures with a contract simulator (reserves, deductions, escalations), automatically associates costs with the applicable royalty periods, and gives artists transparent dashboards into their earnings. In-app artist payouts are powered by Airwallex for secure multi-currency international payments, letting labels pay artists and partners worldwide without juggling separate banking tools. Tone is backed by QED Investors. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC-portfolio lead; Tone is a SaaS application and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Karat.io
providers.description: Karat (trykarat.com) is a fintech platform providing integrated business banking and financial tools built for entrepreneurs, content creators, agencies, and small businesses managing irregular income. Its product suite spans FDIC-insured business checking accounts with high APY, the Karat Card and Karat Max charge/credit cards with rewards and no annual fees, mass and international contractor payments, AI-powered bookkeeping with automatic transaction categorization, invoicing, and multi-entity team management. Surfaced as a portfolio company of ggv-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Karat publishes a consumer web and mobile app but no public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Makrwatch
providers.description: Makrwatch is a creator representation and sponsorship management platform that sits between independent content creators and brands. It sources and filters brand-deal opportunities, negotiates terms and rates, protects creator IP and creative freedom, and handles the administrative work of briefs, timelines, revisions, invoicing, and payment tracking so creators can focus on producing content. Founded out of Y Combinator (W15) and based in New York City, the platform reports $27M+ distributed to creators across 34,000+ sponsorships for 7,400+ creators operating in 118 countries. The company was founded in 2013 as themidgame and still operates its GitHub organization under that name. Makrwatch does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface at this time: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, MCP server or agent card anywhere on its public surface, and its two AWS API Gateway hosts (api.makrwatch.com and platform.makrwatch.com) are private backends for its own Creators and Brands applications, answering every unauthenticated request with HTTP 403.

providers.name: ReDEF
providers.description: REDEF is a media curation and newsletter company founded and led by Jason Hirschhorn (CEO + Chief Curator) that "DJs the internet" — surfacing daily remixes of the stories, people, and ideas that matter across Media, Fashion, Music, Sports, and Tech. Readers follow curated Mixes, Sets, Originals, Charts, and email Newsletters ("interest remixes for curious minds"), and can build and share their own mixes. ReDEF was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a public consumer content website (redef.com) but no public developer program, API, documentation, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: Soundboks
providers.description: Soundboks is a Danish consumer-electronics company that designs and manufactures loud, durable, battery-powered Bluetooth party speakers (Soundboks 4, Soundboks Mix) plus companion products such as Lightboks party lights. Products are sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify-powered storefront and controlled with a companion iOS/Android app that supports wireless playback and multi-speaker pairing (TeamUp). Soundboks does not publish a first-party developer API or SDK; its only programmatic surface is the Shopify Customer Account API (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect) exposed on its own store domain via the standard Shopify discovery documents, which is what this enrichment pass captured.

providers.name: Open Podcast API
providers.description: The Open Podcast API is an initiative aiming to provide a feature-complete synchronization API specification for podcast (web) apps and user-focused servers. The specification covers synchronization of subscriptions, listening progress, favorites, queues, and device state across compliant clients and self-hosted servers, with the goal of giving listeners portable control of their podcast data.

providers.name: 80,000 Hours
providers.description: 80,000 Hours is an independent nonprofit, founded in 2011 by Benjamin Todd and William MacAskill out of Oxford, that provides free research and support to help people use their careers to help solve the world's most pressing problems. The name refers to the roughly 80,000 hours a typical person works over their lifetime. It publishes an evidence-based career guide, in-depth problem profiles, a long-form podcast, and one-on-one advising, and runs a curated high-impact job board at jobs.80000hours.org. Since 2016 it has ranked helping navigate the transition to advanced AI as its top priority. It is a content and career-advice organization rather than an API producer; no public developer API is published, though it does serve a machine-readable llms.txt index of its content.

providers.name: Cameo
providers.description: Cameo is a consumer marketplace for personalized video messages from celebrities, athletes, musicians, comedians, and creators. Fans book a custom shout-out by sending a short script with personal details, and the talent records and delivers a bespoke video, typically within seven days, for occasions like birthdays, milestones, and celebrations. Cameo also runs Cameo for Business for branded talent content, sells gift cards, and offers a Red Carpet Rewards loyalty program. Cameo does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI; this profile tracks the company's public web, help, and security surface.

providers.name: Egab
providers.description: Egab is a journalism platform founded in late 2020 and headquartered in Cairo, Egypt, that connects local journalists across the Global South — the Middle East, Africa, and beyond (60+ countries) — with international media outlets. It specializes in solutions journalism, offering journalists mentoring, editorial support, skills development, and fair compensation from pitch to publication, while giving newsrooms cost-efficient access to authentic, exclusive stories and diverse local contributors without flying in reporters.

providers.name: Fab.com
providers.description: Fab.com is a digital content marketplace operated by Epic Games, where creators buy and sell 3D models, materials, environments, VFX, audio, and game-ready assets. Launched in October 2024, Fab consolidated four of Epic's prior storefronts — the Unreal Engine Marketplace, the Sketchfab Store, Quixel, and the ArtStation Marketplace — into a single catalog with unified licensing, and integrates into Unreal Engine, UEFN, and the Epic Games Launcher. The fabcom entry was originally added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead for the earlier, unrelated Fab.com flash-sale design-commerce company (2011–2015), which wound down before the domain passed to Epic Games; see x-identity-note. Fab publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification as of this pass — the surface captured here is its documentation, support, and security-disclosure posture.

providers.name: Instaread
providers.description: Instaread is a media and audio technology company with two products. Its consumer app delivers ~15-minute audio and text summaries of bestselling books across business, self-help, history, health, politics, and fiction on mobile, tablet, and desktop. Its publisher product, Instaread Player, is a free embeddable audio widget that uses AI text-to-speech (including custom voice cloning) to convert website articles, blogs, and newsletters into natural-sounding audio, monetized for publishers through programmatic audio advertising. The Player is used by 200+ brands, ships ADA/WCAG accessibility support, an analytics dashboard, podcast distribution, and a WordPress plugin, and works on Squarespace, Wix, Webflow, and custom sites via a single embed code. Instaread does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: BallerTV
providers.description: BallerTV (Baller, Inc.) is a Pasadena, California sports media company that live streams and provides on-demand replays and highlights of youth and amateur sports, including basketball, volleyball, soccer, lacrosse, softball, and football, from thousands of tournaments and showcases nationwide. Subscribers range from families following athletes to NCAA and professional scouts using the footage for recruiting and scouting. The platform includes a Game Finder for locating events, purchasable athlete highlight reels, and BTVision, an AI-powered ball-tracking streaming technology that improves the basketball viewing experience. BallerTV is a consumer streaming product delivered through its website and iOS/Android apps; it does not publish a public developer API or SDK program. This profile was surfaced as an index-ventures portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: CD Baby
providers.description: CD Baby is an independent music distribution and publishing administration service for songwriters, performers, and independent record labels. Founded in 1998 and now part of Downtown Music Holdings under Virgin Music Group, CD Baby services over 50 million music assets from creators in hundreds of countries across six continents. The platform distributes music to 150+ digital service providers including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Pandora, Tidal, TikTok, Amazon, Shazam, and Deezer, and is a flagship member of YouTube's Preferred Distributor Program plus a preferred partner with Apple and Spotify. Services include digital distribution, physical CD and vinyl manufacturing, publishing administration, cover song licensing, sync licensing through CDB Boost, YouTube and social monetization, performing rights organization (ASCAP, BMI, SOCAN) registration assistance, and promotion tools via SymphonyOS, HearNow, Show.co, Managed Ads, Groover, Laylo, and Internet Radio Airplay. Pricing is a one-time fee ($9.99 single, $14.99 album) with artists retaining over 90% of earnings. CD Baby has paid out more than $1 billion to artists. CD Baby has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; all distribution and reporting workflows are exposed only through the artist member portal at members.cdbaby.com.

providers.name: roli
providers.description: ROLI (Luminary ROLI Ltd.) is a British music-technology company known for expressive electronic instruments — the Seaboard, LUMI Keys keyboards, and the modular BLOCKS system — together with companion software such as ROLI Dashboard, ROLI Connect, Equator, and ROLI Learn. Its instruments pioneer MPE (MIDI Polyphonic Expression) for per-note pitch, timbre, and dynamics control. For developers, ROLI publishes first-party SDKs under the github.com/weareroli organization — the C++ BLOCKS-SDK and roli_blocks_basics for building applications that talk to BLOCKS hardware, and the archived mpejs library for MPE MIDI in the browser. ROLI is backed by Balderton Capital and Index Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with real developer, SDK, and domain-security artifacts.

providers.name: Grade
providers.description: Grade is the API for performance-based payroll, letting companies pay workers, creators, contractors, and AI agents based on results rather than hours worked. Companies push performance signals into Grade via webhooks or direct API calls (task completed, milestone hit, content published, views tracked, invoice processed), and Grade runs them against configurable payout rules — flat fees, tiered commissions, threshold bonuses, or blended structures — handling the math, de-duplication, and approval workflows automatically. Grade tracks every post across platforms, approves and distributes bulk payouts in one click, and handles compliance end to end: KYC verification, tax-form collection, DAC7 reporting, worker classification, and merchant-of-record services. Payouts reach 190+ countries via local bank transfers, PayPal, Wise, Payoneer, Revolut, Airtm, and USDT, with no separate creator account required. Grade (YC W26) is based in San Francisco and has paid out $10M+ to date.

providers.name: TourHero
providers.description: TourHero is a social travel platform and end-to-end group trip operations partner that lets creators, coaches, and community leaders host fully customized group trips in 50+ countries, with itinerary design, vetted local operators, payments, and on-the-ground logistics handled by TourHero. Travelers can browse and book public trips on its Explore page, and hosts plan for free while TourHero earns commission from local suppliers. Backed by 500 Global and Lightspeed Venture Partners, it is a consumer platform with no publicly documented developer API surface at this time, though it publishes an llms.txt profile for AI agents.

providers.name: Audacy
providers.description: Audacy, Inc. is a U.S. multi-platform audio and entertainment company that operates the country's second-largest radio group alongside the Audacy streaming app, a major podcast network, and the Amperwave audio ad-tech and distribution platform. Formerly known as Entercom (rebranded to Audacy on March 30, 2021), the company filed prepackaged Chapter 11 bankruptcy on January 7, 2024 and emerged on September 30, 2024 as a privately held company after equitizing approximately $1.6 billion of funded debt and reducing total debt from roughly $1.9 billion to $350 million. The current portfolio spans ~230 radio brands across 47 markets, 200+ million monthly listeners, ~2 billion annual podcast downloads, and the Cadence13, Pineapple Street Studios, Podcorn, and BetMGM Network (formerly BetQL) audio brands. There is no public developer API, no published OpenAPI, and no GitHub organization with public repositories; integration is brokered through ad sales, programmatic marketplaces, and the Amperwave platform.

providers.name: Stability Audio
providers.description: Stable Audio (by Stability AI) is a generative audio model for music and sound-effect generation. The Stability Developer Platform exposes Stable Audio 2.5 endpoints alongside image, video, and 3D generation. Pricing is credit-based at 1 credit = $0.01; Stable Audio 2.5 generations are reported at $0.20 per generation regardless of duration.

providers.name: API League
providers.description: API League is a comprehensive API marketplace aggregating 60+ best-in-class APIs across categories including books, news, humor, food, knowledge, art, web, text processing, and media. It offers code examples in 21 languages, SDKs, Postman collections, and free API key access for developers to launch projects quickly.

providers.name: Changelog
providers.description: Changelog is a media company and podcast network for developers covering open source and software development. Founded by Adam Stacoviak and Jerod Santo, Changelog produces world-class developer podcasts including The Changelog, which features deep technical interviews and conversations with the people and teams driving open source software forward. Changelog also publishes a weekly developer news newsletter and operates an open source platform (changelog.com) built with Elixir and Phoenix.

providers.name: Dolby
providers.description: Dolby Laboratories is a leading technology company specializing in audio and video. The Dolby developer platform (dolby.io / Dolby OptiView) provides APIs and SDKs for media processing, real-time streaming, video playback, and ad delivery. Dolby is responsible for technologies including Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Dolby Digital.

providers.name: Equipboard
providers.description: Equipboard is a community-sourced music-gear discovery platform where musicians, producers, and DJs find the equipment behind the music. Members browse the gear their favorite artists play — guitars, effects pedals, synthesizers, DAWs, plug-ins, microphones, drum machines, and keyboards — build and share their own rigs and gear lists, read and write reviews, and follow buy-links to retailers. Equipboard is built by musicians for musicians and monetizes primarily through affiliate relationships (including the Amazon Associates Program). Recent product work adds album- and track-level gear attribution. The company is backed by 500 Global. Equipboard does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network and enriched from Equipboard's public web surface.

providers.name: Anker Innovations
providers.description: Anker Innovations is a global consumer-electronics company headquartered in Shenzhen, China, known for its Anker charging and power products, Soundcore audio, eufy smart-home and security devices, Nebula projectors, and Anker SOLIX portable power and solar storage. Through the Anker Open Platform (developer.anker.com) the company exposes a developer surface that lets partners integrate and control Anker devices from their own applications via API and SDK, gated behind an Open Platform login. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and is being enriched with the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Rephrase.ai
providers.description: Rephrase.ai is a Bengaluru-based generative-AI startup whose text-to-video platform, Rephrase Studio, turns plain text scripts into videos of digital human avatars ("actors") that speak the script with lip-synced, natural voices. It exposed a Rephrase Studio API for programmatic video generation (list actors and voices, create and export videos, poll video status) secured with OAuth2 bearer tokens. Backed by Techstars, Rephrase.ai was acquired by Adobe in November 2023 and its technology folded into Adobe's video and generative-AI offerings; the standalone product hosts have since been decommissioned, though the legacy API reference remains hosted on ReadMe. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist for historical and enrichment purposes.

providers.name: Splice
providers.description: Splice is a New York-based music creation platform serving producers, songwriters, and audio creators. Its core offerings are Splice Sounds, a catalog of millions of 100% royalty-free samples, one-shots, loops, MIDI patterns, and presets sold through a credit-based subscription; Splice INSTRUMENT, a creator-first virtual instrument with monthly free drops and unlimited premium presets via subscription; and a Rent-to-Own Plugins marketplace offering pay-as-you-go full-license access to 130+ professional VST/AU/AAX plugins from third-party vendors such as Xfer (Serum 2), Arturia (V Collection 11 Pro), Spitfire Audio (Abbey Road Two), and XLN Audio (RC-20). Splice ships a desktop app, a mobile app, the Splice Sounds Plugin (beta) for in-DAW browsing, and native integrations for Ableton Live 12.3+, Studio One Pro 7, Studio Pro 8+, and Pro Tools 2025.6+. The revenue model is consumer subscriptions (Sounds+ $12.99/mo, Creator $19.99/mo with 200 credits, Creator+ $39.99/mo with 500 credits, INSTRUMENT $12.99/mo) plus rent-to-own plugin payments. Splice does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or partner program; its GitHub organization at github.com/splice contains internal tooling, GitHub Actions, audio engineering exercises, and forks rather than externally consumable APIs.

providers.name: Dare Drop
providers.description: Dare Drop is a gaming influencer marketing platform that connects game publishers and brands with content creators across Twitch, YouTube, and TikTok. The platform runs reward-driven "Dares" — challenges that incentivize streamers and creators to produce longer, more engaging content around a title, while automating creator targeting, campaign management, and reporting. Dare Drop offers influencer campaigns, ongoing influencer programs, and organic outreach, and has facilitated over 18,000 publisher Dares and distributed more than 30,000 rewards to creator communities. Its customers include game studios and publishers such as EA, Respawn, Raw Fury, Tencent, Obsidian, and Gearbox. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface has been found to date.

providers.name: GigFinesse
providers.description: GigFinesse is a live-entertainment talent booking platform that connects hospitality venues — hotels, restaurants, bars, and clubs — with musicians, DJs, and performing artists. Venues discover and book vetted talent and manage contracts, insurance, scheduling, and payments through a centralized dashboard, while artists gain access to consistent, recurring gig opportunities. Clients include premium hospitality brands such as St. Regis, The Ritz-Carlton, Fairmont Hotels, and Hard Rock Hotel. GigFinesse is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. No public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Intro
providers.description: Intro is a consumer marketplace, founded in 2020 by Raad Mobrem and headquartered in Los Angeles, that connects people with vetted, in-demand experts for one-on-one advice over scheduled video calls. Experts span career and business, interior design and home decor, style and beauty, health and wellness, fitness and nutrition, astrology, and more, with per-session pricing set by each expert. Intro also lets creators and professionals monetize their audience by publishing a bookable profile. The company raised a $10M seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with participation from Seven Seven Six. Intro operates as a consumer web and mobile product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: Kale
providers.description: Kale (operated by Palette Technologies, Inc., dba Kale) is a creator-rewards and user-generated-content marketplace that connects social-media content creators with brands. Creators join brand challenges and tournaments, post authentic sponsored content about products they use, and earn cash, merchandise, and perks; brands source authentic UGC and micro-influencer marketing at scale. The platform is delivered through the getkale.com and kalecard.com web apps and native iOS/Android apps, with a merchant network spanning consumer brands such as Chili's, Planet Fitness, Urban Outfitters, DoorDash, Southwest, and Starbucks. Kale is backed by Forerunner Ventures. No public developer/API surface is published; this profile captures the company's public identity and security posture.

providers.name: KatalistAI
providers.description: Katalist is an AI-powered storyboarding and video platform that turns scripts and ideas into visual stories with consistent characters and scenes. Founded in 2023, it converts scripts (CSV, Word, PowerPoint) into storyboards in one click, keeps characters consistent across shots, lets creators customize framing, angles, poses and scenes, and includes a video studio that layers voiceover, music and sound effects. It targets filmmakers, directors, advertisers, content creators, animators and educators looking to move from concept to visualized story faster. Backed by 500 Global, Katalist is a consumer/creative generative-AI SaaS accessed through its web application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Luel
providers.description: Luel is a two-sided marketplace and multi-modal data lab for AI training data, connecting companies that need high-quality, rights-cleared datasets with verified contributors who supply and license on-demand video, audio, and image data. Contributors can earn money by submitting media from their own devices (for example, footage from their camera roll) or by completing requested data tasks, while buyers purchase premium, curated, rights-cleared multimodal datasets from the Luel catalog. Positioned as "the frontier of data," Luel powers the foundations of machine perception through a proprietary, continuous data engine. The company is backed by Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Luel does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Novel Effect
providers.description: Novel Effect is a Techstars-backed interactive read-aloud technology company whose voice-recognition platform listens as a person reads a children's picture book aloud and plays perfectly synchronized music, sound effects, and character voices in response, turning any book into an immersive shared experience. Delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps, Novel Effect is used by families, teachers, and libraries to make reading aloud more engaging for young children. Novel Effect is a consumer and education (EdTech) product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Publishizer
providers.description: Publishizer is a book crowdfunding platform and literary agency that connects authors with readers and publishers. Authors create book proposals and run pre-order campaigns; readers pre-order copies to signal demand; and publishers use data such as pre-order volume and proposal quality to discover and acquire promising manuscripts. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer web platform and blog but no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Smiler
providers.description: Smiler is an Amsterdam-based on-the-spot photography marketplace that connects travelers and consumers with a network of professional freelance photographers at popular tourist hotspots and leisure locations worldwide. Founded in 2020, Smiler lets people book fast, affordable photoshoots in advance across 100+ destinations, with photos delivered within 48 hours and free cancellation up to 24 hours before the shoot. The company also operates the Smiler Photographer Suite, an all-in-one tool for photographers to build portfolio websites, manage bookings, deliver mobile-friendly client galleries, and handle payments. Smiler is trusted by tens of thousands of photographers across 50+ countries and is backed by Speedinvest, Mosaic Ventures, Dutch Founders Fund, and PROfounders.

providers.name: Wave
providers.description: Wave is a virtual entertainment company that produces interactive, avatar-driven virtual concerts and immersive live music experiences known as "Waves." The platform streams stylized, real-time performances from major recording artists — including The Weeknd, Justin Bieber, John Legend, J Balvin, and Alison Wonderland — as animated avatars across VR headsets, desktop, mobile, and social video platforms, letting fans attend and interact with shows from anywhere. Wave is a consumer-facing entertainment and media product (accessed at wavexr.com) rather than a developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation. It was surfaced as a venture-portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, where this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: alphin
providers.description: alphin is a Berlin-based marketing platform for local small businesses, giving restaurants, cafes, salons, and similar SMBs an all-in-one app to manage and automate their online presence. Its product suite spans review collection (alphin Reviews), Instagram and social management (alphin Socials), professional photography (alphin Photos), local influencer marketing (alphin Local Influencers), targeted Instagram advertising (alphin Local Ads), and multi-platform profile management across Google, TripAdvisor, and Yelp (alphin Portals), consolidated into one dashboard with daily reporting and analytics. Founded in 2016 (as Freachly GmbH), alphin serves 1,000+ local businesses across Germany, Austria, the UK, and Israel, and is backed by HV Capital, Partech, Scale Capital, and Wille Finance. alphin publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; the product is delivered through its web and mobile Business App.

providers.name: Jays
providers.description: JAYS is a Swedish consumer audio brand founded in 2006 by Jens and Johan, headquartered in Sweden and owned by the Northbaze Group AB. It designs and sells wireless and wired headphones, true-wireless earbuds, Bluetooth and multiroom speakers, and audio accessories, sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at jaysheadphones.com. JAYS publishes no first-party developer API; its only machine-accessible surface is the Shopify-provided agent-commerce layer: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with a hosted MCP shopping endpoint, Customer Account OpenID Connect / OAuth discovery documents, and an llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio/commitment lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Podcast API
providers.description: An API for developers to get information on over 4 million podcasts, 180 million episodes, and 1.5 million transcripts. Powered by Taddy's GraphQL API, the Podcast API supports search across podcast series, episode details, transcripts, top charts, popularity data, and webhook subscriptions.

providers.name: Universal Music Group
providers.description: Universal Music Group N.V. (UMG) is the world's largest music company, headquartered in Hilversum, Netherlands with operational headquarters in Santa Monica, California. Spun off from Vivendi and listed on Euronext Amsterdam (ticker: UMG) on September 21, 2021 at a EUR 54 billion valuation, UMG operates Recorded Music, Music Publishing (Universal Music Publishing Group / UMPG), and Merchandising (Bravado), plus film and television production (PolyGram Entertainment) and the artist services and catalog arm Universal Music Enterprises. The company is led by Chairman and CEO Sir Lucian Grainge. Major label families include Republic Corps (Republic, Island, Def Jam), Interscope Capitol Labels Group (Interscope, Geffen, A&M, Capitol, Blue Note, Motown), Virgin Music Group, Verve Label Group (Verve, Decca, Deutsche Grammophon, Impulse!, Philips), UMG Nashville (MCA Nashville, Mercury Nashville, EMI Records Nashville, Capitol Records Nashville), Universal Music Latin Entertainment, and Universal Music UK. Catalog scale exceeds 3 million recordings and 4 million compositions. Ownership is split among Bolloré / Vivendi (~28%), Tencent Music (~11%), Pershing Square (~10%), and the public float. UMG operates no public developer portal: catalog and metadata reach developers only indirectly through downstream DSPs (Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Amazon Music) and through partner / aggregator programs (7digital exposed UMG catalog under a partner API; that integration is the only third-party developer-facing surface that has ever been openly documented). Royalty and publishing portals (UMG Royalty Portal, UMPG Window) exist for songwriters and rights holders behind authentication, not as APIs. AI is the active integration vector in 2025-2026: UMG has announced licensed generative-music partnerships with Udio, Splice, KLAY Vision, SoundLabs, ProRata, BandLab, YouTube, TikTok, Meta, and KDDI, and has filed 15+ AI patents with Liquidax Capital across collaboration, rights management, music & health, and AI threat protection. These integrations operate through bilateral commercial agreements, not a self-serve developer program. The official Universal-Music-Group GitHub organization (created May 15, 2024) has 0 public repositories.

providers.name: Baton Media
providers.description: Baton is a music collaboration and IP-management platform for unreleased music, built by Baton Media Inc. (New York, Techstars '23). It gives musicians, producers, managers, and talent scouts tools to securely upload, organize, version, and share unreleased tracks, beat packs, and sample libraries across iOS and web. A proprietary media player shows creators exactly who is listening to their material, while collaboration spaces (private, invite-only, or public), an in-app audio studio (looping, pitch shifting, EQ, effects, sample pairing), and a creator-to-fan marketplace support discovery, placement opportunities, and monetization. Baton is building collaboration protocols to track IP rights and automate crediting and compensation across the creator economy. As of this enrichment the company publishes a consumer product (iOS app + web) with no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Bindery
providers.description: Bindery (Bindery Books) is a community-driven, influencer-led book publishing platform and marketplace founded by Matt Kaye and Meg Harvey. It pairs established book "tastemakers" — social-media book reviewers and BookTok / Bookstagram creators — with emerging authors, letting each tastemaker run their own micro-imprint (Ezeekat Press, Boundless Press, Skies Press, and others), acquire titles, weigh in on creative decisions, and promote them to their communities in exchange for a share of net earnings. Often described as "Patreon meets publishing," Bindery combines traditional trade distribution and marketing with paid membership communities, a bookshop, exclusive reviews and author interviews, and iOS and Android apps. The company is backed by Bloomberg Beta.

providers.name: DubClub
providers.description: DubClub is an all-in-one platform to create and join sports betting communities. It is a marketplace connecting sports betting content creators known as cappers or handicappers with subscribers who want timely, reliable betting picks and analysis. Creators monetize their expertise by selling picks and predictions through paid subscriptions, while subscribers receive content directly via notifications and messaging rather than scattered across social media and Discord. DubClub has facilitated tens of millions in payments for creators and delivered hundreds of millions of messages containing informational sports betting content. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital; DubClub publishes a consumer web product and does not expose a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: dwell
providers.description: Dwell is a digital publication and lifestyle brand focused on modern home design, architecture, and interior inspiration, published by Ziff Davis. It offers curated home tours, architectural features, renovation and before/after projects, design photography, real estate listings, shopping guides, and design news, plus a Dwell+ subscription for ad-free access and subscriber exclusives, a shop for furniture and decor, and a "Find a Pro" professional directory. Dwell was surfaced as a portfolio-adjacent lead in the API Evangelist network; the public dwell.com property is a consumer media site with no developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so no API artifacts are captured for it.

providers.name: Merchbar
providers.description: Merchbar, Inc. is the official merchandise retailer for top musicians, selling vinyl records, CDs, t-shirts, hoodies, posters, and other band merchandise across thousands of artist storefronts at merchbar.com. It runs a consumer shopping experience alongside a "Merchbar for Artists" program and official merchandise integrations with YouTube and Spotify. Merchbar is a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital. As of this enrichment pass Merchbar publishes no public API, developer program, SDKs, or technical documentation — no developer/api/docs subdomain resolves and there is no /.well-known/security.txt — so this profile captures only its public web presence and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Pixyalbum
providers.description: Pixyalbum is a Mexican consumer photo-printing service that turns digital photos from a mobile device into physical printed products delivered across Mexico. Its catalog includes Fotolibros (soft- and hard-cover photo books of 40-100 pages), Imanes (packs of square photo magnets), and Pixycuadros (photographic prints with optional framing). Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Pixyalbum is a direct-to-consumer product with no public API, developer portal, or documentation at the time of enrichment; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

providers.name: SmartShoot
providers.description: SmartShoot is a San Francisco-based (founded 2012) photography and video production platform that connects enterprises and marketing teams with a managed network of more than 200,000 professional photographers and videographers to produce custom, on-brand photo and video content at scale. The web-based platform coordinates shoot booking, project collaboration, editing, and cloud-based delivery across many locations, serving e-commerce, real estate, and multi-location brands such as Google, YouTube, Uber, Expedia, and Yelp. SmartShoot is a B2B managed-service marketplace with no publicly documented developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal as of this enrichment pass; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Svbtle
providers.description: Svbtle is a minimalist publishing and blogging platform designed to work the way your brain does, pairing a distraction-free Markdown editor with a simple dashboard for organizing drafts, developing ideas, and publishing to a clean reading experience. Created by Dustin Curtis and operated by Neutral Corporation, Svbtle emphasizes longevity through its "Forever Promise" that published writing remains permanently accessible online. Svbtle is a subscription-based writer's network rather than a developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, OAuth authorization server, or .well-known metadata, and each blog is exposed only as a human-readable site with an RSS feed.

providers.name: DICE
providers.description: DICE is a mobile-first live events discovery and ticketing platform founded in London in 2014 by Phil Hutcheon. Through the DICE app (iOS and Android) and dice.fm, fans discover concerts, club nights, festivals, tours and livestreams, buy fee-transparent tickets that live securely in-app, join waiting lists for sold-out shows, and resell tickets at face value to curb touting. DICE also runs a partner business serving venues, promoters, artists and festivals with tools to reach fans, sell tickets and grow their audiences, and owns the Boiler Room brand. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, DICE operates across the UK, Europe and the US. DICE publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, security and legal surface.

providers.name: Duetti
providers.description: Duetti is a New York-headquartered music finance and catalog services company founded in 2022 by Lior Tibon and Christopher Nolte that buys music rights directly from independent artists, songwriters and creators. Artists earning at least $2,000 a year from tracks at least six months old can sell masters, publishing shares or a percentage of their royalties for an upfront cash payment — no debt, interest or recoupment — while keeping whatever they do not sell. Alongside the catalog purchases Duetti provides distribution, royalty tracking and claiming, playlisting across a network of owned Spotify playlists, sync placement, paid advertising, influencer and UGC campaigns, and a commissioned remix program. The company has raised more than $435 million, works with 1,100+ music creators, and publishes the Music Economics Report and the Billboard Music Finance Index. Duetti operates artist-facing web applications (DUO onboarding, statements vault, sync portal) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract as of this profile.

providers.name: Groover
providers.description: Groover is a music promotion platform that connects independent artists and their representatives with a network of more than 3,000 vetted music-industry professionals — playlist curators, bloggers, journalists, radio stations, record labels, and managers. Artists submit a track and spend credits ("Grooviz", roughly €2 each) to reach individual curators, and Groover guarantees personalized feedback within seven days or refunds the credit. Founded in Paris in 2018, the company also operates Temple by Groover, a fanbase-growth toolset. Groover runs a consumer web application on a credit-based, pay-per-submission model and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Reedsy
providers.description: Reedsy is a marketplace and toolset for authors and publishers, connecting writers with a curated network of more than 3,700 vetted publishing professionals including editors, book designers, marketers, ghostwriters, web designers, and translators. Beyond the marketplace, Reedsy offers Reedsy Studio (a free writing and book-formatting application), Reedsy Learning (courses and events), Reedsy Discovery (book reviews), and Reedsy Prompts (weekly writing prompts). It supports authors across the full self-publishing journey from manuscript development through market launch. Reedsy is backed by Seedcamp and publishes no public developer API today.

providers.name: Sol
providers.description: Sol Reader is a wearable e-reader — marketed as the world's first wearable e-reader — built by Sol and backed by Initialized Capital. The device is a lightweight (104g) headset with dual 1.3" 271ppi side-lit E Ink displays, adjustable diopter optics and IPD, a handheld remote, and 25+ hours of battery for a distraction-free reading experience. It reads a connected Kindle library and DRM-free EPUB uploads, offers the Sol Store with over one million titles, plus AI question-answering and an AutoPilot speed-reading mode. Sol is a consumer hardware company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Planetary
providers.description: Planetary is a decentralized, peer-to-peer social networking company built on the Secure Scuttlebutt (SSB) protocol, offering an iOS app for algorithm-free social media where users own and store their data locally with no advertising and no data selling. The team has since migrated its design, app, and philosophy to the Nostr protocol under a new app, nos.social. The project is fully open source, developed in the open on GitHub, and is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. Planetary exposes no commercial REST/HTTP API; its developer surface is the underlying SSB/Nostr protocol documentation (RPC methods, replication, blobs) rather than a hosted web API.

providers.name: Kuli
providers.description: Kuli is an AI agent for influencer marketing, built for consumer brands. It runs the full creator marketing lifecycle end to end — discovery, vetting, outreach, and reporting — so a small marketing team ships like a much larger one. Unlike platforms that filter creators on metadata such as follower counts and engagement rates, Kuli's agent watches actual creator videos frame by frame across TikTok and Instagram, assessing brand safety, content style, audience signals, and brand fit, then drafts personalized outreach in the brand's own voice and reports campaign ROI on a schedule. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Levallois-Perret, Paris, Kuli is a Y Combinator company. As of this profile Kuli publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs — its only machine-readable surface is an llms.txt.

providers.name: Artifact
providers.description: Artifact is a consumer service that captures and preserves family stories through professional, guided interviews. The company conducts remote 30-minute interviews with a family member and edits each one into a studio-quality ~20-minute audio episode, hosted on a private webpage where relatives can add photos and share the recording. Episodes are priced per interview, positioning the product as a way to record a loved one's life story and memories. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) in the consumer sector. As of 2026 the company announced it is winding down: new Artifacts are no longer sold, and previously purchased interviews may be scheduled through October 31. The service exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Lala
providers.description: Lala (meetlala.io) is an AI content platform for educators that turns recordings of online classes into publishable social media content. Instructors either host lessons natively on Lala's own video-call product or upload an existing recording by file or link, and Lala automatically curates short-form Reels in Instagram and TikTok aspect ratios, assembles packaged courses, and returns a transcription and summary after each class. It is sold in three tiers -- Free, Pro and Enterprise -- metered on upload minutes, video-call participants and Reels generated per class, and is aimed at tutors, music instructors, teacherpreneurs, schools and universities. Lala is a 500 Global portfolio company that came out of the 500 Georgia program. As of July 2026 Lala publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable API description.

providers.name: Likeable Local
providers.description: Likeable Local is a social media marketing company that now operates publicly as Storytellit — likeablelocal.com and www.likeablelocal.com both redirect to storytellit.com, while the product application at app.likeablelocal.com and app.storytellit.com still identifies itself as "Likeable Local" in its web app manifest. Storytellit sells social media management as a white-label service to digital agencies — strategy, custom content creation and publishing, paid social advertising, lead capture, and monthly performance reporting for the agency's clients, across verticals including dental, medical, legal, real estate, insurance, finance, eCommerce, and local business. The company is based in Portland, Maine, and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Likeable Local / Storytellit publishes no public API, no developer portal, no API documentation, and no machine-readable specification; the public web surface is a four-page marketing site plus a private, login-gated React application. A production API does exist but is an internal application backend rather than a developer product — api.storytellit.com and api.likeablelocal.com both resolve to the same Amazon load balancer and run Express over FeathersJS, and every service path, including a GraphQL endpoint, rejects anonymous callers with HTTP 401 while serving no specification and no documentation of any kind.

providers.name: 9GAG
providers.description: 9GAG is a Hong Kong-based global entertainment platform founded in 2008 with the mission to "make the world happier." It is one of the largest meme and user-generated humor communities on the internet, distributing funny images, GIFs, and videos across its website and iOS/Android apps to an audience of 150-200 million people and billions of monthly video views. 9GAG operates consumer-facing products (the 9GAG feed, 9GAG Pro subscription, and related community features) rather than a public developer API program; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed company (500 Global, Y Combinator, Freestyle Capital, True Ventures, First Round Capital, Greycroft) and has been enriched with its real public web, policy, and security surfaces. No official public API or developer portal is published as of this enrichment; the community libraries that exist are unofficial and reverse-engineered.

providers.name: Barnes & Noble
providers.description: Barnes & Noble is the largest retail bookseller in the United States and the operator of the Nook digital reading platform. Barnes & Noble does not currently publish a public general-purpose developer portal. Trade and affiliate partners integrate through B&N's affiliate program, the B&N Press self-publishing platform for independent authors, EDI-based wholesale channels with publishers, and the Nook content distribution and reading ecosystem.

providers.name: Memorick
providers.description: Memorick is a 500 Global-backed company operating a live web application at memorick.com. Based on its observable application surface, it is a destination photography booking platform connecting customers with photographers across destinations, handling packages, orders, reviews, coupons, and messaging. The product is built on Laravel (Inertia.js single-page front end) and exposes an OAuth2 authorization server via Laravel Passport (authorize/token/clients/scopes plus personal access tokens), Sanctum first-party session auth, and optional two-factor authentication. It publishes no public API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; the /api/* routes back the first-party application and are authentication-gated. This profile was enriched from live probing of the public surface.

providers.name: Skool
providers.description: Skool is an all-in-one community platform that combines discussion communities, online courses, live calls, and gamification in a single product, founded by Sam Ovens and popularized in partnership with Alex Hormozi. As of this review, Skool does NOT publish an official public or partner developer REST API. The only official programmatic surface is a Zapier integration, gated to the paid Pro plan, that exposes a small set of triggers and actions via a per-group API key used solely to link a Skool group to Zapier - it is not a general-purpose developer API. All broader "Skool API" offerings found in the wild (Apify actors, docs.skoolapi.com, reverse-engineered clients, Chrome extensions) are unofficial third-party tools built on Skool's undocumented internal endpoints and are not endorsed or supported by Skool. This catalog entry is an honest gated stub: no public API surface is modeled because none is documented.

providers.name: BuzzFeed
providers.description: BuzzFeed Inc. is a digital media company founded in 2006 and headquartered in New York City, best known for its viral entertainment, quizzes, pop-culture coverage, and commerce content. The company operates a portfolio of brands including the flagship BuzzFeed site, the news operation HuffPost, and the food brand Tasty, and produces video, podcasts, and shoppable content across web and social platforms. BuzzFeed is a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: BZFD) and monetizes through advertising, brand partnerships, and commerce. It does not publish a general-purpose public developer API program; its public machine-readable surface consists of content syndication (RSS feeds), an advertising/partnerships business, and a security.txt vulnerability-disclosure program via HackerOne. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from an a16z portfolio lead and enriched with the provider's real public surface.

providers.name: Discz
providers.description: Discz is a consumer mobile application that blends music discovery with social chat, styled as a modern, MySpace-inspired music community. Users discover songs, build music profiles, and chat with others around shared taste in music. The iOS app is developed by Discz, a Y Combinator-backed startup and a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. Discz publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its surface is the consumer iOS app distributed through the Apple App Store.

providers.name: DZone
providers.description: DZone is one of the world's largest online communities and a leading publisher of knowledge resources for software engineering professionals. Founded in 1997 with roots in Javalobby, DZone reaches millions of developers each month with articles, tutorials, research guides, and Refcards covering topics including cloud architecture, Java, JavaScript, microservices, containers, data, DevOps, AI, and more.

providers.name: HYPERZ AI
providers.description: HYPERZ AI is a generative-AI company focused on professional photography and headshot generation, offering both consumer (B2C) and enterprise (B2B) products. Its consumer tool, Business Photo AI (businessphoto.ai), turns selfies into professional headshots with customizable poses, outfits, and backgrounds. Its enterprise product, HYPERTURE (hyperture.ai), delivers consistent, studio-grade headshots for teams with brand-consistency controls, member approval workflows, and C2PA provenance verification. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or /.well-known discovery surface — the products are end-user applications rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Mozart AI
providers.description: Mozart AI is a generative audio workstation and AI music-creation platform (mozartai.com) that lets musicians compose, produce, and distribute songs using AI-assisted and agentic tools. Rather than generating finished tracks from a single prompt, it operates as a full digital audio workstation built around context-aware stem generation, real-time MIDI suggestions, synth and effects generation, and automated production tasks such as quantization and time-stretching, letting users work at the level of stems, instruments, or individual notes. Founded in 2025 and based in London, the company raised a $6M seed round led by Balderton Capital in February 2026 and reports more than 100,000 artists and over 1 million songs created. The product is delivered as a consumer web and mobile app (built on the ElevenLabs Eleven Music API) and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Pic-Time
providers.description: Pic-Time is an online gallery, proofing, and print-sales delivery platform for professional photographers - client galleries, slideshows, an integrated print store, and studio-management integrations. Pic-Time does not publish a public developer API, API reference, or OpenAPI specification. Automation is limited to a Zapier integration (three triggers - New Gallery Visitor, New Order Placed, Main Client Gallery Invite Sent - and one action, Create New Gallery) plus private, bilaterally-arranged partner integrations (HoneyBook, Studio Ninja, Light Blue, StyleCloud, the Pic-Time Connect WordPress plugin) that are not documented for third-party developers. No API keys, endpoints, or SDKs are published for general developer use.

providers.name: The Atavist
providers.description: The Atavist is a pioneering digital longform-storytelling brand founded in 2009 by Evan Ratliff, Jefferson Rabb, and Nicholas Thompson. It comprises The Atavist Magazine, which publishes one immersive work of narrative nonfiction each month and has earned National Magazine Award and Emmy recognition, and the Atavist multimedia publishing platform for building rich, media-driven stories. Automattic (the company behind WordPress.com) acquired both the magazine and the platform in 2018; the platform's storytelling features were folded into WordPress.com and the magazine now runs on Newspack by Automattic. The Atavist exposes no public developer API or documented developer program — it is a reader-facing publication at magazine.atavist.com.

providers.name: DistroKid
providers.description: DistroKid is a Brooklyn, New York based digital music distribution service founded in 2013 by Philip Kaplan that lets independent musicians and labels upload an unlimited number of songs and albums to Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, TikTok, Instagram, Pandora, Tidal, Deezer, and dozens of other streaming and download stores for a flat annual subscription fee while keeping 100% of their royalties. By 2020 the platform was distributing roughly a third of all new music released worldwide and serving more than two million artists; Spotify and Insight Partners both hold equity stakes following a 2021 valuation around $1.3B. Around the core distribution product DistroKid has built out a suite of artist services including Teams for automated royalty splits, cover-song mechanical licensing, YouTube Content ID monetization, DistroVid music-video distribution, Upstream label matching, Mixea AI mastering, and DistroKid Direct for fan merchandising and pre-orders. The company has historically operated without a public developer API — integrations with stores, DSPs, rights organizations, and partners are handled through private B2B arrangements, and the only public web endpoints exposed under distrokid.com/api are unauthenticated pre-save widgets used to drive Spotify follow/save campaigns. DistroKid is actively hiring API engineers to scale partner and AI-facing integrations, suggesting a more formal developer surface may emerge, but as of 2026 there is no published OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, sandbox, or developer portal. Third-party reverse-engineered wrappers such as the unofficial Golang `distrogo` library exist but are not endorsed.

providers.name: TuneCore
providers.description: TuneCore is a Brooklyn, New York based independent music distribution and publishing administration company founded in 2006 (as YourTunes, Inc., rebranded TuneCore in 2008) and acquired by French music company Believe in 2015. TuneCore lets self-releasing artists and labels deliver recorded music to 150+ digital stores and streaming services — Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, TikTok, Tidal, Deezer, Beatport, and others — while retaining 100% of their rights and master ownership, in exchange for a flat annual distribution fee starting at $24.99/year for unlimited releases. TuneCore Publishing Administration registers compositions with performance rights organizations, mechanical rights societies, and digital service providers worldwide to collect songwriter royalties, sync, and neighboring rights income. Additional services include the TuneCore Accelerator artist development program, TuneCore Social (monetization on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts), TuneCore Direct Advance (royalty-backed capital, powered by RoyFi), mastering, and Splits for collaborator revenue sharing. TuneCore operates across 5 continents with local teams in 15+ countries through Believe's global network. There is no current public TuneCore developer API, SDK, or partner portal — an earlier white-label REST/XML "TuneCore Direct" partner API existed circa 2008-2012 (with a community Ruby gem `tunecore_direct`) but is no longer actively documented or promoted. TuneCore's public-facing surface is the artist web app at web.tunecore.com and the support/help center; any current B2B integrations run through Believe's enterprise partnerships.

providers.name: Humans Anonymous
providers.description: Humans Anonymous is a consumer mobile application offering anonymous audio spaces for mental health and peer support, built on the premise that "being a human is hard" and no one should face it alone. Distributed as an iOS app, it lets people join anonymous, real-time audio rooms to talk and listen around mental wellbeing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes a consumer product website (humansanon.com) with privacy and terms pages but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Pratilipi
providers.description: Pratilipi is India's largest digital storytelling platform, democratizing story creation and consumption across languages, formats, and boundaries. Built by Nasadiya Technologies Private Limited and headquartered in Bangalore, it lets more than 300,000 self-published writers reach roughly 25 million monthly readers across twelve Indian languages (Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi, Bengali, English, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Urdu, and Odia). The ecosystem spans Pratilipi Literature, Pratilipi FM (audio books, podcasts, and folk songs), Pratilipi Comics (the largest Hindi online comic platform), Westland Publications, and IVM Podcasts, carrying a story "from someone's draft to someone's screen." Pratilipi does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's identity, web properties, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Art19
providers.description: Art19 (ART19, Inc.) is a podcast hosting, distribution, and monetization platform, and an Amazon company. It provides publishers, networks, and enterprises with a content management system for audio, automated RSS feed generation, dynamic ad insertion and targeting through its WarpFeed feed technology, and an embeddable Web Player. The platform serves podcast delivery, analytics, and advertising workflows at scale.
