providers.name: Printique
providers.description: Printique (An Adorama Company, formerly AdoramaPix) is a professional online photo lab based in Brooklyn, NYC that produces photo prints, fine-art giclee prints, photo books, albums, wall decor (metal, acrylic, canvas, glass, framed, wood), cards, calendars, and photo gifts. Printique does NOT publish a documented public developer or fulfillment API. There is no developer portal, no published REST reference, no API keys, and no OpenAPI definition on the open web. Programmatic and automated ordering is instead delivered through prebuilt partner-platform integrations - a Squarespace integration that syncs products and automates order fulfillment, a PhotoShelter wholesale print-and-product integration for professional photographers, Fundy Designer album integration, and desktop plugins for Adobe Lightroom and Capture One that publish images directly to Printique. A Pro membership tier ($14.95/month or $159.95/year) unlocks tiered wholesale savings, white-label blind shipping, and dedicated support for photography businesses. The logical API surfaces below (catalog, orders, order status) are honestly modeled from Printique's public product, Pro, and integration pages to describe how ordering works conceptually; they are NOT transcribed from any released or documented Printique API. No public endpoints, paths, or request/response schemas are published, so endpointsModeled is true and no endpoint surface has been fabricated beyond these named, integration-delivered capabilities.

providers.name: Epic! Creations
providers.description: Epic! Creations, Inc. operates Epic, an award-winning digital reading and learning platform for children twelve and under. The service gives families and educators unlimited access to a library of more than 40,000 books, audiobooks, and learning videos, with reading-level personalization, quizzes, and progress tracking. Epic offers a consumer family subscription and Epic School, a version that is free for teachers and students during the school day via class codes. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Epic is a business-to-consumer application and does not publish a public developer program, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Kobalt Music
providers.description: Kobalt Music Group is a music services company providing publishing administration, neighbouring rights and recordings services for songwriters, artists, publishers and rights holders. It collects, matches and accounts for royalties across streaming and digital platforms, reporting to clients through its own portals rather than a public developer program. Kobalt's rights and content management platform is operated by KTech, its technology arm, which processes the micro-transaction royalty data behind Kobalt Music Publishing and AMRA, the global digital collection society. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass Kobalt publishes no public API, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification; the only public machine-readable surface found was an RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: Lunar-X
providers.description: Lunar-X (Lunar X) is a global digital content studio that acquires, develops, and operates creator-driven entertainment brands into globally recognized franchises across animation, educational content, functional music, ecommerce, and live events. Its properties include Economics Explained, Theorist Inc, Music Labs, and Lunar Kids, collectively spanning tens of billions of views and over a hundred million subscribers. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Creandum and added to the API Evangelist network. As a media/content operator it publishes a marketing website and privacy policy but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Pocket Fm
providers.description: Pocket FM is an audio entertainment platform offering long-form audio series, audiobooks, and serialized stories across genres such as romance, fantasy, thriller, and horror. Listeners stream free episodes and unlock premium content through an in-app coins/store model, while writers and voice creators publish original work through the Pocket FM Studio. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass, Pocket FM operates as a consumer-facing mobile and web product and does not publish a public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: SFX
providers.description: SFX (SFX Entertainment, now operating as LiveStyle, Inc) is a Beverly Hills based global live-events and electronic dance music company. Originally founded by Robert F.X. Sillerman as a roll-up of EDM festival and event brands, the company reorganized as LiveStyle and continues to produce live music experiences, festivals, and fan events under the banner "For the Love of Music." It was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company presents a corporate marketing web presence and publishes no public developer, API, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Take Two
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO) is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment for consumers worldwide, headquartered in New York City. The company delivers its products principally through three wholly owned labels — Rockstar Games, 2K, and Zynga — spanning console, PC, and mobile platforms via physical retail, digital download, online platforms, and cloud streaming. Franchises include Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption, NBA 2K, Borderlands, and mobile titles such as Words With Friends and Toon Blast. Take-Two is a publicly traded interactive entertainment holding company; it does not publish a public developer API program, developer portal, or API documentation at the corporate level. This profile was surfaced as a general-catalyst job-board listing and carried into the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment found no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: DataSift (MediaSift Inc.)
providers.description: DataSift (MediaSift Inc.) was a pioneering social data platform that provided real-time and historical access to social media firehoses (Twitter, Facebook Topic Data, and more) through its CSDL filtering language and its Push, Historics, and Managed Sources REST APIs. Founded in 2007 and backed by Insight Partners and others, the company was acquired by Meltwater in 2019; the datasift.com domain now redirects to meltwater.com and the standalone DataSift developer platform and APIs have been discontinued. Official first-party client SDKs for Python, Ruby, PHP, Java, and Node.js remain published on public package registries under the datasift GitHub organization as historical artifacts.

providers.name: Callisto Media
providers.description: Callisto Media Inc. was a data-driven nonfiction book publisher founded in 2011 by chief executive Benjamin Wayne, operating from 1955 Broadway in Oakland, California (earlier Emeryville) and 220 West 19th Street in New York. It built a publishing model around demand signals rather than editorial instinct — mining point-of-sale data, search volume and category gaps to decide which instructional titles to commission, then matching each topic to a subject-matter author. Its primary imprint was Rockridge Press, best known for diet-, appliance- and condition-specific cookbooks and health titles, alongside the Callisto Kids line of pre-K through grade 12 workbooks, STEM, history and biography titles; the company said it had reached more than 50 million customers and ranked among the top fifteen US publishers by unit sales. It raised venture funding from 137 Ventures in 2017, then contracted sharply — cutting 35 percent of staff in July 2022 and a further 200 roles that October — and on 9 May 2023 its publishing assets were acquired by the independent publisher Sourcebooks in a deal funded by Penguin Random House, with Simon & Schuster Distribution Services continuing to distribute the titles. The brand now trades as Callisto Publishing, a Sourcebooks imprint: callistomedia.com 301-redirects to callistopublishing.com, which 301-redirects again to sourcebooks.com/callisto (chain verified 2026-08-02). Callisto Media is a consumer publishing business, not a software vendor, and has no public API surface. Probes on 2026-08-02 against callistomedia.com, www.callistopublishing.com and www.sourcebooks.com returned no machine-readable contract: /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /.well-known/ai-plugin.json all 404, /.well-known/agent-card.json and /.well-known/agent.json both 404 (no A2A agent card), and every other probed path answered with the Sourcebooks single-page Magento storefront shell rather than a document. There is no developer portal, no GitHub organization (callistomedia, callisto-media and rockridgepress all 404 on the GitHub API), no published SDK on npm or PyPI, and no llms.txt.

providers.name: RedNote (Xiaohongshu)
providers.description: RedNote, known in China as Xiaohongshu (小红书, "Little Red Book"), is a Shanghai-based social and e-commerce platform operated by Xingyin Information Technology (行吟信息科技). It blends user-generated lifestyle content, community discovery, and in-app shopping, and is one of China's largest content-commerce platforms. Beyond the consumer app, RedNote runs an open platform (open.xiaohongshu.com) plus the Qianfan (千帆) merchant commerce workbench (ark.xiaohongshu.com) and a mini-program surface (miniapp.xiaohongshu.com) that let brands, merchants, and marketing partners integrate storefronts, content, and campaigns. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of HongShan (Sequoia China) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Drop
providers.description: Drop (formerly Massdrop) is a consumer e-commerce brand operated by Corsair that sells limited-edition, community-driven products across mechanical keyboards, audiophile gear, and licensed gaming collaborations (Fallout, Cyberpunk 2077, The Witcher, Call of Duty and others). Founded in San Francisco and backed by Cowboy Ventures and other investors before its acquisition by Corsair, Drop runs a direct-to-consumer storefront at drop.com with a Zendesk-based support helpdesk. It is a retail brand with no public developer API program; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company in the network.

providers.name: Playback
providers.description: Playback (playback.tv) is a mobile-first live streaming platform backed by Khosla Ventures, where creators broadcast live streams, audiences watch and interact in real time, and streamers earn through the platform's monetization program. The consumer product is organized around streaming, watching, earning, and community guidelines. As of this enrichment pass Playback publishes a consumer web/app experience and a Notaku-powered help center but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented developer surface; this profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Verso Corporation
providers.description: Verso Corporation (NYSE: VRS) was a North American producer of coated papers including coated groundwood, coated freesheet, and specialty products used in magazines, catalogs, commercial print, books, and packaging. Headquartered in Miamisburg, Ohio, Verso operated mills in Wisconsin Rapids (Wisconsin), Escanaba (Michigan), Duluth (Minnesota), and historically Luke (Maryland). In March 2022, Swedish pulp and paper group BillerudKorsnäs (now Billerud) completed its acquisition of Verso for $825 million in cash, taking the company private and rebranding it as Billerud Americas Corporation. The Verso standalone brand, ticker, and corporate web presence have been retired; ongoing North American operations, paper grades, and customer relationships now sit inside Billerud's global business.

providers.name: Knowable
providers.description: Knowable was a mobile audio-learning company that united world-class experts, thinkers, and storytellers to produce structured audio courses for curious minds — an "audio courses" take on online learning delivered as serialized lessons rather than one-off podcasts. Founded by the Bit Kitchen team and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z led its round in May 2019), Knowable published expert-led course series across business, creativity, and personal development. The company is no longer operational: knowable.fyi now serves a tombstone notice stating that Knowable has been acquired by Medium and directing former listeners to Medium.com. Knowable never published a public developer program, API, SDKs, or developer documentation, and its GitHub organization (bitkitchen) exposes no public repositories. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record from the a16z portfolio; there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Stan
providers.description: Stan (stan.store) is an all-in-one creator storefront and link-in-bio commerce platform that lets creators sell digital products, online courses, coaching calls, memberships, and webinars directly from a single mobile-first store link. The platform bundles checkout and payments, email marketing, an AutoDM tool, analytics, and integrations with third-party tools such as Zoom and Google Meet. Backed by Forerunner Ventures, General Catalyst, and Norwest Venture Partners, Stan targets the creator economy. As of this enrichment pass Stan publishes no public developer API, webhook specification, or SDKs — the surface is a consumer product plus a help center; this profile captures the identity and a probed domain-security profile.

providers.name: uberVU
providers.description: uberVU was a social media analytics and monitoring company, backed by Seedcamp, that offered brand-insight dashboards and a metrics API before being acquired by Hootsuite in 2014. The company no longer operates independently - ubervu.com now 301-redirects to blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-analytics/, its former metrics API is retired, and its GitHub organization is dormant. This profile is kept as a historical record of a VC-portfolio company with no current public API surface.

providers.name: Viacom
providers.description: Viacom was an American mass media conglomerate that merged with CBS Corporation in December 2019 to form ViacomCBS (later rebranded as Paramount Global). The combined entity, which included brands such as CBS, MTV, Nickelodeon, Comedy Central, BET, Paramount Pictures, Showtime, and Paramount+, was subsequently acquired by Skydance Media and ceased to exist as an independent public company in August 2025. Viacom maintained open source software through its GitHub organization (ViacomInc), including tools for Roku channel development, tvOS UI components, and broadcast calendar utilities. No public external developer API program was offered.

providers.name: Famebit

providers.name: Gaspack
providers.description: Gaspack is a Web3 NFT launchpad that helps brands, creators, and artists turn their intellectual property into NFT projects and bridge them with their fans. The platform provides a full technology stack, community management, and creative consultancy that supports projects from ideation through minting, launching, scaling, and long-term maintenance as sustainable digital-collectible businesses. Gaspack operates a consumer application (app.gaspack.xyz) for collecting digital assets and has incubated branded NFT collections such as JPG People, Easy Demons Club, and Jukiverse, alongside Kometh, a Web3 comic publishing and discovery platform. Gaspack is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Gaspack publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its verified public identity only.

providers.name: ByteDance
providers.description: ByteDance is a global technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Beijing, operating across roughly 120 cities with more than 150,000 employees. providers.name: Caffeine
providers.description: Caffeine was a social broadcasting and live-streaming platform founded in 2016 by former Apple designers Ben Keighran and Sam Roberts, and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Greylock Partners. Built on a proprietary WebRTC-based real-time video distribution network, Caffeine positioned itself as a low-latency, social-first alternative to Twitch for gaming, entertainment, and — in its later years — live sports, partnering with roughly 200 sports organizations and reaching tens of millions of monthly users. The company published open-source broadcasting tooling under its caffeinetv GitHub organization (libcaffeine, caffeine-rtc, an OBS plugin, and the CaffQL GraphQL code generator) but never shipped a public, documented developer API program. Caffeine announced it was ceasing operations, and its web presence is now a shutdown notice; this profile is retained as an a16z portfolio lead and is archival rather than an active, integrable API provider.

providers.name: Klout
providers.description: Klout was a San Francisco social-analytics company, founded in 2008 by Joe Fernandez and Binh Tran, that scored individuals on their online social influence. The "Klout Score" was a single number from 1 to 100 derived from the size of a person's social network and how other people engaged with the content they published across connected accounts such as Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, and Google+. Klout operated a public REST API — the Klout API v2 at api.klout.com — that let developers resolve a social handle to a Klout identity, look up a user's score and score history, and retrieve influence graphs (who a user influences and is influenced by) and topic affinities; access was key-based and widely used by marketing, CRM, and social-listening tools, and a large community of third-party client libraries grew up around it in Ruby, Node.js, Python, and PHP. Lithium Technologies acquired Klout on 27 March 2014 for approximately $200 million. Lithium retired Klout as a standalone service on 25 May 2018 — the day the EU General Data Protection Regulation took effect — stating that Klout's AI and machine-learning capabilities were valuable to Lithium but the consumer service was not aligned with its long-term strategy. The Klout API was shut down with the service. Lithium has since been rebranded as Khoros, and klout.com now redirects into the Khoros website. The company is defunct and operates no live API; this profile is retained as a historical provider record in the API Evangelist network.

DataRank was acquired by Simply Measured in 2015, which was in turn acquired by Sprout Social in 2017. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API; datarank.com redirects to sproutsocial.com and ttagg.com is parked.

Qiming Venture Partners lists FangTek in its portfolio as "a leading provider of highly integrated circuit solutions for cell phone, portable device, voice processing, audio processing and image processing." FangTek is a silicon component vendor that reaches customers through electronics distributors; it publishes no public developer platform, web API, SDK or machine-readable API surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security data only.

providers.name: Adim
providers.description: Adim is an entertainment-technology and web3 media company co-founded in 2022 by It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia creator Rob McElhenney alongside Richard Rosenblatt, Chase Rosenblatt, Melissa Kaspers, and Spencer Marell. Adim invites a community of storytellers, writers, and fans to collaboratively create, develop, and co-own a new generation of intellectual property — stories, characters, and narrative universes known as the Adimverse — rewarding contributors with ownership stakes and a say in how the community is governed. The company raised a $5M seed round led by Chris Dixon of a16z crypto. Adim is a consumer creative platform rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Catalog
providers.description: Catalog was a music distribution and direct-to-fan platform that let independent musicians sell digital downloads while keeping 100% of earnings, collect fan emails directly, split revenue with collaborators, run referral rewards, and control private, public, or scheduled releases with zero marketplace fees. The company has ceased operations - its homepage now shows a closure announcement - and it never published a public developer API, SDKs, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Cord *
providers.description: Cord * (Cord Project Inc.) was a consumer communication startup building simple, fast voice messaging that let people send short audio clips to one friend or broadcast to a whole group, delivered through iOS and Android mobile apps. Backed by GV and Index Ventures, the New York based team was acquired by Spotify in 2015, where the product formed the foundation of a group exploring new ways people interact with audio; the standalone apps and service were subsequently wound down. The company never published a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record with no active API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Graham Holdings
providers.description: Graham Holdings (NYSE: GHC) is a diversified holding company with operations in education, television broadcasting, digital media, manufacturing, healthcare, automotive, restaurants, and custom framing. Principal subsidiaries include Kaplan (educational services), Graham Media Group and Social News Desk (broadcasting and social media tools), The Slate Group and Foreign Policy (digital publishing), Code3 and City Cast (digital marketing and local news), Hoover Treated Wood Products, Joyce/Dayton, Group Dekko, and Forney (manufacturing), Graham Healthcare Group (home health and hospice), Graham Automotive (dealerships), Clyde's Restaurant Group (including Old Ebbitt Grill), and Framebridge (online custom framing). No public developer APIs have been identified across the portfolio.

providers.name: Happs
providers.description: Happs was a live-streaming platform for creators and citizen journalists that let broadcasters produce real-time news and multicast a single live stream simultaneously to Facebook, YouTube, Twitter/X, Twitch and other destinations, with built-in studio tools and viewer monetization through tips and monthly sponsorships. Originally launched as a home for independent journalists, it expanded into a general creator social network and ran its live video on Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS). The company raised roughly $4.7M in a post-seed round led by Bullpen Capital and Crosslink Capital, and wound down operations around 2022. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead record; no public developer program, API, or live web surface remains.

providers.name: Hearst
providers.description: Hearst is a privately held, diversified American media, information, and services conglomerate headquartered in the Hearst Tower in New York City. Founded in 1887 by William Randolph Hearst, the company spans more than 360 businesses across magazines, newspapers, broadcast television, cable networks, business and financial information, healthcare information, automotive data, and venture investments. Hearst reported approximately US$13B in revenue (2024) with ~22,000 employees worldwide.

providers.name: Massive Science
providers.description: Massive Science is a science communication platform and media company that publishes stories, explainers, lab notes, and reports about current research, written and edited by working scientists. It runs the Massive Science Consortium, a training network of scientist-writers, alongside editorial content, newsletters, a community discussion forum, and a shop. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment finds no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface beyond a public RSS feed.

providers.name: PaceMaker
providers.description: PaceMaker is the consumer DJ application from Pacemaker Music AB, a Swedish startup and 500 Global portfolio company, that lets anyone mix and mash millions of tracks on iPhone and iPad. It connects to streaming catalogs such as Spotify, includes an AI DJ that suggests matching tracks and beat-matched transitions, and lets users crop and blend songs at phrase, bar, and beat precision to record and share their own mixtapes. Pacemaker is a mobile end-user product; as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal, and its domain (pacemaker.net) currently serves a WordPress marketing blog.

Operated by TechNexus Venture Collaborative, which has backed 600+ startups since 2007, Podfund pairs funding with business planning, a peer community, mentor matching, a growth toolkit, and partner offers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and added to the API Evangelist network. Podfund publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and web presence for network discovery.

providers.name: Roll
providers.description: Roll was a social token infrastructure platform for the creator economy, letting creators and communities mint and manage their own branded ERC-20 tokens on the Ethereum blockchain. Founded in 2017 in New York City and backed by Techstars, IOSG Ventures, and Fabric Ventures (a $10M Series A), Roll offered developer APIs and OAuth-based integrations so third-party apps could query tokens and balances. The custodial Roll app and its developer API (docs.tryroll.com / api.tryroll.com) were sunset in April 2025 and permanently shut down on 2025-05-26; the company web surface no longer resolves. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; this pass confirms the company is defunct with no live API surface remaining.

providers.name: Smule
providers.description: Smule is an American consumer music technology company whose flagship social singing and karaoke app lets people perform solos, duets, and group songs and collaborate with other singers around the world in real time. Launched on iOS in 2012 and on Android in 2013 under the name "Sing! Karaoke," the app grew to tens of millions of monthly active users. Smule Inc. is headquartered in San Francisco and is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Shasta Ventures. Smule publishes no official public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: 555 Comic
providers.description: 555 Comic is an interactive storytelling and virtual-influencer studio founded by Ben Watanabe. It runs casts of anime-styled virtual characters — such as @CRC_Luna — who publish real-time alternate-reality-game (ARG) stories across TikTok, Twitter/X and Instagram, letting fans create original characters (OCs) and interact with official storylines across four interconnected fictional worlds: Conspiracy Research Club, All Night Arcade, The Convenience Store, and a Paranormal Research Club. Stories unfold in real time on "Poppy-valley Standard Time," with fans participating through social comments. 555 Comic is a Techstars Music portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe of its web host.

providers.name: 60dB
providers.description: 60dB was a personalized short-form audio and podcast application built by Tiny Garage Labs, founded in 2016 by John Ciancutti, Steve Henn, and Steve McLendon. The app curated and recommended short radio-style audio stories tailored to a listener's habits, and was available on iOS, Android, and the web as well as through Alexa, Android Auto, and CarPlay. It was backed by Bloomberg Beta, Khosla Ventures, and Rivet Ventures. Google acqui-hired the founding team in October 2017 and the 60dB service was shut down on November 10, 2017. The company is defunct and publishes no developer program, API, or machine-readable interface today; the 60db.com domain now resolves to a parked placeholder page. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Adphorus
providers.description: Adphorus was an Istanbul- and Berlin-based travel marketing-science company and an official Facebook and Instagram Marketing Partner (certified since 2014) that specialized in automated, scalable Dynamic Ads for Travel, helping brands such as Expedia, Trivago, and Kayak scale full-funnel performance on Facebook and Instagram. The company was acquired by Sojern in November 2017 and subsequently absorbed; it operates no independent public website or developer API today, so this network profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record rather than an active API provider. The enrichment pipeline found no live domain, developer portal, or specification to harvest.

providers.name: Anchor *
providers.description: Anchor was a podcast creation, hosting, distribution, and monetization platform (anchor.fm), founded in 2015 and backed by GV (Google Ventures) among others. Spotify acquired Anchor in 2019 and folded it into its creator tooling, later rebranding the product to Spotify for Podcasters and then Spotify for Creators. The anchor.fm domain now 302-redirects to Spotify's creator product (podcasters.spotify.com / creators.spotify.com); Anchor never published a standalone public developer API, and it no longer operates as an independent company. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead; enrichment confirms it is an acquired/absorbed brand with no independent developer surface to harvest.

providers.name: Anchor FM
providers.description: Anchor FM was a podcast creation, hosting, distribution, and monetization platform founded in 2015 that let anyone record, edit, publish, and monetize a podcast for free from a phone or browser. Spotify acquired Anchor in 2019 and folded the product into Spotify for Podcasters, later rebranded Spotify for Creators; the anchor.fm domain now redirects to creators.spotify.com. Anchor never published a public developer API or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity and domain-security posture only. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel (consumer sector).

providers.name: AppBistro
providers.description: AppBistro, operated by MMTG Labs, was an application marketplace for the Facebook Pages platform that let brands and page administrators discover, install, and manage third-party apps to boost engagement and reach on their fan pages. It also built AppGalleries, a white-label app-store platform. A TechCrunch Disrupt 2010 finalist, the San Francisco startup raised a $550K convertible note (Sand Hill Angels, 500 Startups, i/o Ventures, Zelkova Ventures, Seraph Group, and angels including Alfred Lin) and was acquired by mobile ad network InMobi on 2012-07-13, after which the product and its five-person team (co-founders Ryan Merket and Nalin Mittal) wound down. The company is defunct and appbistro.com no longer resolves; no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: Appionics
providers.description: Appionics Holdings Limited is a Hong Kong mobile applications and games company that operated under the consumer brand name "Animoca". Co-founded by Yat Siu and David Kim, and emerging out of the Outblaze group, Appionics developed and published cross-platform games and apps for iOS and Android, claiming more than 150 titles and over 40 million downloads during 2011. In 2014 the company spun off part of its app portfolio, along with a set of licensed intellectual-property game rights, into Animoca Brands Corporation Limited (ASX AB1), which listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in January 2015 and later pivoted to blockchain gaming and NFTs. Appionics itself never published a developer program, and today has no live web or API surface of its own.

providers.name: Associated Content
providers.description: Associated Content was an open content publishing platform founded in 2005 by Luke Beatty that paid contributors to publish articles, video, audio, and images on any topic, then distributed that library through associatedcontent.com and a network of syndication partners. At its peak it hosted over one million pieces of content from roughly 250,000 contributors and adopted Thomson Reuters OpenCalais for automated classification of that library. It raised a $5.4M Series A from SoftBank Capital (2006), a $10M Series B from SoftBank, Canaan Partners, and Tim Armstrong (2007), and $6M more in 2009, before Yahoo acquired it in May 2010. Yahoo rebranded the property as Yahoo Voices in December 2011 and shut it down on July 31, 2014, retiring the Yahoo Contributor Network the following month. The company is defunct: it never published a public developer API, and associatedcontent.com is now a parked domain that refuses HTTPS.

providers.name: Avnera
providers.description: Avnera Corporation was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon, that designed low-power analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits and audio system-on-chip (SoC) solutions for wireless headphones, headsets, soundbars, speakers, and gaming audio devices. Backed by venture investors including Redpoint Ventures, Avnera was acquired by Skyworks Solutions in 2017 and now operates as part of Skyworks. It maintains no independent developer program or public API surface; the avnera.com domain resolves to a parked/inactive page with no product site.

providers.name: Axiometrix Solutions
providers.description: Axiometrix Solutions is a global test and measurement company serving technology-intensive industries through three specialist brands - GRAS Sound & Vibration (acoustic and vibration sensors for challenging environments), imc Test & Measurement (modular data acquisition, signal conditioning, and shock/vibration solutions), and Audio Precision (audio and RF analyzers for quality validation). Its integrated portfolio of sensors, data acquisition systems, control software, analysis software, and test fixtures supports advanced research, R&D, and production/manufacturing test across aerospace, defense, automotive, consumer electronics, audiology and medical technology, communications, semiconductor, and environmental monitoring markets. Backed by Battery Ventures. No public web API or developer program has been identified for this provider.

providers.name: Backtype
providers.description: BackType was a San Francisco social-media analytics startup (backed by 500 Startups/500 Global) whose BackTweets product helped publishers measure the reach and conversion of their Tweets and content for clients including The New York Times, HubSpot, bitly, and SlideShare. The BackType team also built Storm, the distributed real-time stream-processing system later open-sourced as Apache Storm. Twitter acquired BackType on July 5, 2011 and folded the team into its platform group; the standalone product and public API were discontinued after the acquisition. The company is defunct and backtype.com is now a parked domain, so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Beast Industries
providers.description: Beast Industries is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of social-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: creator-economy. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Blinkist
providers.description: Blinkist is a Berlin-founded subscription learning app that condenses the key ideas of thousands of nonfiction books and podcasts into roughly 15-minute text and audio summaries called "Blinks." Launched in 2012, it is used by millions of readers to learn on the go across categories such as productivity, business, psychology, personal growth, and science, and it also offers Blinkist for Business for teams and organizations. The consumer product is delivered through the web and iOS/Android apps backed by a private mobile backend at api.blinkist.com; Blinkist does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal. Blinkist was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by Insight Partners) and enriched with the provider signals that could be verified from its public surface.

providers.name: Bluefin Labs
providers.description: Bluefin Labs was a social TV analytics company founded in 2008 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Deb Roy and Michael Fleischman, spun out of research at the MIT Media Lab. Its platform semantically interpreted public social media commentary from Twitter, Facebook and blogs and automatically linked those comments to the television shows and advertisements people were watching, producing audience engagement measurement for networks, agencies and brands. Its product, Bluefin Signals, gave media buyers a tool for accessing and analyzing social TV response data. The company raised a Series A led by Redpoint Ventures in 2010 and a $12M Series B led by Time Warner Investments in January 2012, with SoftBank Capital and Lerer Ventures participating. Twitter acquired Bluefin Labs on February 6, 2013 for a reported ~$100 million and absorbed the team and technology into its TV advertising and analytics products. The company is DEFUNCT: it operates no independent product, developer program or API, and the bluefinlabs.com domain no longer belongs to the company — it now redirects to an unrelated news site. This profile is retained as a historical / portfolio-graph record only.

providers.name: Bop.fm
providers.description: Bop.fm was a music-sharing and playlist startup that let people share and play individual songs across streaming services — building a link for a track that would resolve to whichever service (Spotify, Deezer, SoundCloud, YouTube, Rdio) each listener used. Founded out of Y Combinator, it reportedly reached several million monthly listeners and raised roughly $2M before being acquihired by identity-protection company LifeLock in October 2015, at which point the website, mobile apps, and embedded players were shut down. The company is defunct: the bop.fm domain no longer serves the product (it now redirects to an unrelated parked site) and no developer portal, documentation, or API surface remains online. This profile is retained as a historical record within the API Evangelist network; there are no live API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Braid
providers.description: Braid Networks was a creator-economy startup that let creators build customizable landing pages unifying their work across the web (blog posts, videos, podcasts and commerce links), build mailing lists, and engage followers via text and push notifications. Founded by former Facebook product designer Matthew Cahill and software engineer Chris Piro, it raised a $6.8M seed round from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Initialized Capital. Braid was a consumer direct-to-fan product and never published a public developer API. The company was acquired by Laurel on 2026-01-01 to power Laurel's Signal product and has since shut down; the braid.network domain no longer serves a site.

providers.name: Bridgeco
providers.description: BridgeCo Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2000 that built networked-audio silicon and software for consumer electronics. Its JukeBlox platform — a system-on-a-chip paired with a software development kit — let wireless speakers, A/V receivers, home-theater systems and docking stations stream music from tablets, smartphones and PCs, and was designed into products from Pioneer, Philips, Denon, Marantz, JBL and Harman/Kardon. Earlybird Venture Capital was the company's first institutional investor in 2000. BridgeCo was acquired by Standard Microsystems Corporation (SMSC) on 19 May 2011 in a deal worth up to $67.5 million, and SMSC was in turn acquired by Microchip Technology on 2 August 2012, where the JukeBlox wireless-audio line was folded into Microchip's portfolio. BridgeCo no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, documentation or public API; the bridgeco.com domain today is an unrelated domain-for-sale parking page.

providers.name: Buddy Media
providers.description: Buddy Media was a social media marketing and advertising platform (founded 2007, backed by ggv-capital, insight-partners and ivp) that helped brands manage publishing, engagement and paid campaigns across Facebook, Twitter and other social networks. It was acquired by Salesforce in 2012 and folded into the Salesforce Marketing Cloud (Social Studio) product line; the buddymedia.com domain now redirects to salesforce.com/marketing. No standalone Buddy Media public API, developer portal or first-party SDK remains — this network entry is retained as a historical martech company stub.

providers.name: Cakeshop
providers.description: Cakeshop is a commerce-enablement platform that helps creators monetize their expertise, selling digital products, courses, and services directly to their audiences. It was a San Francisco-based startup operating in the creator-economy and content-monetization space, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass its public site (getcakeshop.co) returns an expired Squarespace notice, and no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or GitHub organization could be discovered; the domain still resolves over TLS and was probed for baseline security posture.

providers.name: Callin
providers.description: Callin was a social podcasting and live-streaming platform founded by David Sacks and Axel Ericsson, backed by Craft Ventures, that let creators stream live audio, take listener questions, then record, edit, publish and share the result as a podcast episode. The company was acquired by Rumble (NASDAQ: RUM) in May 2023 and the standalone consumer app was subsequently wound down. As of enrichment the callin.com domain returns only a Cloudflare-gated placeholder and the provider exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface to enrich.

providers.name: Canvas Networks
providers.description: Canvas Networks was a consumer social media and image-sharing startup founded by Christopher "moot" Poole (the founder of 4chan). Launched in private beta in early 2011 at canv.as, the platform let users share, annotate, and remix images on moderated, topic-based boards, positioning itself as a friendlier, more creative take on imageboard culture. It raised roughly $3.6M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Union Square Ventures, SV Angel, Lerer Ventures, Founder Collective, Ron Conway, and Joshua Schachter, and later pivoted to the mobile drawing app DrawQuest. The company shut down on January 21, 2014, citing its inability to build a sustainable business model. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirms it is defunct with no surviving developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: chushou
providers.description: Chushou (触手TV / 触手直播) was a China-based mobile game live-streaming platform, at one point among the largest mobile-focused game streaming services in China, letting players broadcast and watch mobile gameplay. It was backed by Qiming Venture Partners and Tencent and is surfaced here as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass the company's public web presence at chushou.tv is unreachable (the server returns empty replies) and it exposes no documented developer API, SDK, or portal, so this profile remains an inactive/defunct lead with no live API surface to enrich beyond DNS/TLS-level signals.

providers.name: Conexant Systems
providers.description: Conexant Systems, Inc. was an American fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California. Spun off from Rockwell Semiconductor Systems in 1999, it designed mixed-signal and system-on-chip products for audio, voice, imaging, modem, and networking applications, and was best known for its dial-up modem chipsets, audio codecs, and far-field voice-input processors used in smart-home and IoT devices. Conexant's audio and imaging business was acquired by Synaptics in 2017 and the standalone Conexant brand has since been retired. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; the company publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface (its former conexant.com domain no longer resolves to an active site), so there are no API artifacts to enrich at this time.

providers.name: Conteller
providers.description: Conteller is a user-generated content (UGC) marketplace where brands pay for authentic media directly from their own customers and everyday, non-famous creators. Brands publish media briefs and the platform lets creators capture, submit, and store photos, videos, and TikTok-style content, then handles paying those creators for approved submissions. A Mexican/Spanish startup (Madrid) selected for Batch 19 of 500 Global's Somos Lucha accelerator program in Latin America, Conteller has run pilots spanning roughly 1,400 creators and a dozen brands. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of 500 Global. The public site is no longer serving: conteller.com and www.conteller.com both return HTTP 402 "Payment required / DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED" from Vercel on every path, the blog subdomain returns a Cloudflare 1014 and the admin subdomain a 522, and the Internet Archive holds no successful capture of the site after 2025-07-16. No public developer portal, API, documentation, OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or agent-card surface has ever been found for Conteller, and its GitHub organization publishes no repositories.

providers.name: cordproject
providers.description: Cord Project Inc. was a New York based startup founded around 2014 by former Google Creative Lab designers Thomas Gayno and Jeff Baxter. Its flagship product, Cord, was a voice messaging app that let people send short audio clips as a middle ground between texting and phone calls. The company raised seed funding from investors including Google Ventures, Greycroft, Lerer Hippeau, Metamorphic Ventures and Slow Ventures, and was acquired by Spotify in January 2016 to explore new ways of interacting with audio. There is no public developer API, SDK, or documentation; this profile is retained as a Slow Ventures portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Crossref Metadata Search
providers.description: Books & Articles Metadata

providers.name: Crowdamp
providers.description: Crowdamp is a privately held Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company co-founded by Ruben Mayer-Hirshfeld and Alexandra Botez. The company built SuperFan, a creator-economy messaging product that let fans text their favorite social media stars and receive a personalized reply, using natural language processing to help those creators respond efficiently at scale across their whole audience. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass Crowdamp publishes no developer surface of any kind: there is no developer portal, no documentation, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, no SDK packages in any public registry, and no working product website. The SuperFan domain superfanapp.com no longer resolves to the product and is listed for sale through a domain reseller, indicating the product is no longer operating. This profile is retained as a portfolio-graph record rather than as an API provider.

providers.name: Crystal
providers.description: Crystal (Crystal Semiconductor) was a hardtech company that designed audio and mixed-signal semiconductor chips. Kleiner Perkins partnered with the company in 1986 at the early stage, and Crystal was subsequently acquired by Cirrus Logic. The company was surfaced from the Kleiner Perkins portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. It operated as a fabless chip designer rather than a software or platform business, and no longer exists as an independent entity: it publishes no website, no developer portal, and no public API surface of any kind. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record and is not an API provider.

providers.name: Curio Labs
providers.description: Curio (curio.io), operated by Curio Labs, was a London-based audio-journalism subscription app founded in 2016 by Govind Balakrishnan and Srikant Chakravarti. It turned articles from premium publishers into professionally narrated audio and later added AI-generated personalized episodes. Backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), EarlyBird, Draper Esprit, Cherry Ventures and Horizons Ventures, it raised over $15M before the founders wound the company down after eight years, citing AI and big-tech competition; they have since moved on to a new venture (Gibran). Enrichment probe finds no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface — curio.io now serves a closure/landing page only.

providers.name: Custom Chat API | MirrorFly
providers.description: MirrorFly is a self-hosted CPaaS providing token-authenticated REST Chat Platform APIs (User and Admin) plus SDKs for in-app chat, HD video/voice calling, VoIP, contact center, chatbot/conversational AI, and live streaming for web and mobile apps.

providers.name: Dangdang
providers.description: Dangdang (当当, dangdang.com) is a Chinese business-to-consumer e-commerce company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Beijing. It began as one of China's largest online booksellers and expanded into a broad general-merchandise marketplace spanning books, e-books and e-readers, digital reading, consumer electronics, apparel, home goods, and maternal and baby products. Once listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker DANG) before being taken private, Dangdang was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. No active public developer program, open platform, or machine-readable API surface was reachable during enrichment (the site is geo-restricted); this profile carries a probed domain-security posture and awaits any discoverable API artifacts.

providers.name: docin
providers.description: docin (豆丁网, docin.com) is a Chinese C2C document-sharing platform operated by Beijing Docin Century Network Technology (北京豆丁世纪网络技术有限公司) that faces the global market. The platform hosts over 1.3 billion documents, books, magazines, and publications spanning education, architecture and construction, business and contracts, medical and psychological materials, industry reports, and legal documents, supporting both learning and practical application. It offers a "豆丁书房" (Docin Reading Room) mobile reading app and VIP membership tiers. docin was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Probing found no public developer or API platform: open.docin.com 301-redirects to the homepage, /app/api returns 404, and no /.well-known discovery documents are published.

providers.name: Drippi
providers.description: Drippi (trydrippi.com) was a New York City-based platform that helped young content creators navigate the complexities of running their creator businesses. The company has been acquired and has closed its service to both current and new customers, directing its community to Instagram (@trydrippi) for future updates. It does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. NOTE FOR ENRICHMENT — this entity is distinct from the similarly named drippi.ai, a separate, bootstrapped Twitter/X cold-outreach DM automation SaaS (founded 2021 by Alex Penunuri, no venture funding); do not attach drippi.ai's API artifacts to this Bloomberg Beta portfolio profile.

providers.name: Drivetime
providers.description: Drivetime (Drive.fm) was a voice-activated, hands-free in-car entertainment platform founded in 2018 by Niko Vuori, Justin Cooper, and Cory Johnson (veterans of Zynga and Rocket Games). The consumer mobile app delivered interactive trivia games, storytelling, quizzes, news, and audiobooks designed to be safe to play while driving, running on Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, and partnered with the Jeopardy game show for a channel narrated by Alex Trebek. The company raised roughly $15M across seed and later rounds, with backing from Canaan Partners, Makers Fund, the Amazon Alexa Fund, Google Assistant Investments, Sinai Ventures, Fuel Capital, and Access Ventures. Drivetime was a business-to-consumer product and never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; as of this profiling the drive.fm / drivetime.fm domain and the associated App Store and Google Play listings no longer resolve, indicating the product has been discontinued.

providers.name: Dulcetta
providers.description: Dulcetta is the company behind Focus@Will (focusatwill.com), a functional-music streaming service that curates instrumental soundtracks scientifically designed to improve concentration and productivity during focused work. Backed by 500 Global, Dulcetta operates a consumer subscription product marketing measurable gains in focus for knowledge workers, students, and creative professionals who work with music. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced lead; no public developer API or documentation surface has been identified to date, so this profile carries company identity and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: EDGE Sound Research
providers.description: EDGE Sound Research is an audio technology company building intelligent audio infrastructure, as stated by its own tagline. Backed by Techstars, the company operates from edgesoundresearch.com. As of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API, SDK, CLI, MCP server, or machine-readable specification (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI) was found on its web presence, and the site is a fully client-rendered Next.js application. This profile captures the company's identity and web/domain security posture within the API Evangelist network pending any future developer surface.

providers.name: Encore Music Technologies
providers.description: Encore Music Technologies, Inc. ("Encore") is a consumer live-music technology company based in Los Angeles, California, founded in 2020 by Ian Edelman, Jonathan Gray, and recording artist Kid Cudi. Its mobile app lets artists perform live inside custom augmented-reality environments directly from a phone while fans join, react, and pay artists in real time through gamified microtransactions such as a ten-cent "clap." The company raised a $9M seed round led by Battery Ventures in February 2022, with participation from 468 Capital, Kayak Ventures, Parade Ventures, and others. Encore ships consumer iOS and Android apps rather than a public developer platform; as of this pass it exposes no documented public API, and its marketing website (clapforencore.com) does not currently resolve to a live server.

providers.name: Facet
providers.description: Facet was a consumer AI image-editing and creative tool, backed by Accel and originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment pass, its domain facet.ai (HTTP) 301-redirects to www.vsco.co/features/canvas ("VSCO Canvas | AI Mood Board Maker for Photographers"), indicating the product has been acquired by / absorbed into VSCO. Facet exposes no independent developer platform, public API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface of its own; its HTTPS endpoint is unreachable.

providers.name: Fanbridge
providers.description: FanBridge was an email and SMS marketing platform for musicians, artists, bands, and creators, letting them grow and message their fan mailing lists, run newsletters, and capture subscribers from shows and social channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-19) confirmed FanBridge is defunct - it was acquired by Kit (formerly ConvertKit) and ceased operations on April 11, 2022, with active accounts migrated to the Kit platform. The domain fanbridge.com now 302-redirects to kit.com/fanbridge. There is no standalone FanBridge developer API, documentation, SDK, or event surface; the developer docs linked from the destination site belong to Kit, not FanBridge.

providers.name: Fanhouse
providers.description: Fanhouse was a creator-subscription social platform, backed by a16z, that let fans pay creators directly for exclusive posts, photos, and community access rather than through ad-driven feeds. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The original product operated at fanhouse.app, which no longer resolves to the company (it now redirects to an unrelated domain), indicating the a16z-backed platform is defunct. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or other machine-readable API surface could be located for the original Fanhouse product, so no scored API artifacts could be produced without fabrication. This profile is retained as a company/lead record.

providers.name: Flipagram
providers.description: Flipagram is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Flye
providers.description: Flye was a San Francisco social-audience and brand-marketing analytics startup (500 Global / 500 Startups Demo Day Batch 19, founded 2016) that helped brands build and understand their audiences from social data (an "audience fingerprint") and run targeted, personalized engagement campaigns using machine learning. The company appears defunct — its original domain (flye.co) has lapsed and now hosts an unrelated online-casino review/affiliate site. No developer platform, API, documentation, SDK, or other technical surface exists for this provider, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest without fabrication.

providers.name: Fortunes
providers.description: ForTunes was a Vienna-based mobile music data analytics application for self-publishing and DIY artists, managers, and small labels. The app collected and visualized performance data across Spotify, Apple Music, SoundCloud, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and other platforms into a single intelligent feed, with notifications for playlist adds and follower growth, a Spotify playlist recommendation engine, public artist profiles, and team collaboration. Backed by Speedinvest (2018), the company was acquired by Utopia Music in 2023. As of this profile the primary web domain (fortunes.io) no longer resolves and no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; the product surface is the consumer iOS and Android apps.

providers.name: Frame
providers.description: Frame Technology Corp. was a software company that developed FrameMaker, a structured desktop-publishing and technical-documentation authoring application widely used for long, complex documents. Founded in the 1980s and taken public, Frame Technology was acquired by Adobe Systems in 1995; FrameMaker continues today as an Adobe product. This is a historical/acquired portfolio company of Canaan Partners with no independent developer or API surface of its own.

providers.name: Friendster
providers.description: Friendster is a mobile-first social network for real-life friends, operating at friendster.com with a native iOS app and a web experience. The service positions itself around privacy and intentional design — no ads, no algorithms, no spam, and an explicit promise never to sell user data — and centers on connecting people with the friends they actually know in real life. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass Friendster publishes a consumer marketing site and a native iOS app, but exposes no public developer program, API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — so there are no API artifacts to harvest, only company identity and live domain-security posture.

providers.name: Gaana
providers.description: API to retrieve song information from Gaana

providers.name: Get Satisfaction
providers.description: Get Satisfaction was a customer-community and engagement SaaS platform that gave companies a hosted online community where customers, employees, and prospects could ask questions, report problems, share ideas, and offer praise in public topic threads. Founded in 2007, it popularized the customer-powered support community model and offered widgets, community moderation, and integrations that companies embedded on their websites and product pages. Get Satisfaction was acquired by the social customer experience management company Sprinklr in 2015 and folded into Sprinklr's platform; the standalone product and its developer program have since been discontinued. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record (backed by Uncork Capital); it no longer operates a live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Gimme Media
providers.description: Gimme Media is the Techstars-backed music company behind Gimme Radio, the heavy-metal streaming and live-DJ radio platform that later expanded into Gimme Metal and Gimme Country. The standalone streaming apps were wound down, and the brand now operates as a Shopify-hosted storefront at gimmemetal.com selling vinyl, merchandise, and exclusive releases to the metal community. As of this enrichment pass Gimme Media publishes no first-party public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI definition, or developer documentation; the only machine-readable surfaces served at its domain are the Shopify Customer Accounts platform OIDC endpoints, which belong to the hosting platform rather than to a Gimme Media API.

providers.name: Gnip
providers.description: Gnip was a social media data aggregation company founded in 2008 in Boulder, Colorado by Eric Marcoullier and Jud Valeski. It became the first authorized reseller of the Twitter "firehose" and delivered enterprise-grade access to real-time and historical social data from Twitter, Tumblr, WordPress, Disqus, StockTwits and many other sources through products such as PowerTrack, Historical PowerTrack, the Search API, the Audience API and the Engagement API. Twitter acquired Gnip in April 2014 and folded its technology into Twitter's enterprise data platform; the Gnip brand and standalone APIs were retired and gnip.com now 301-redirects to the Twitter/X enterprise developer documentation. This profile is preserved for historical/network completeness — Gnip is no longer an independent provider.

providers.name: Group Nine Media
providers.description: Group Nine Media was a New York-based digital-media holding company formed in 2016 through the merger of Discovery Digital with the original Group Nine, uniting the news brand NowThis, the animal brand The Dodo, the lifestyle brand Thrillist, and the science brand Seeker under one roof (it later added PopSugar). Backed by Discovery Inc. and venture investor IVP, it built large social-video and branded-content audiences before it was acquired by Vox Media in February 2022 and folded into that portfolio. Group Nine operated as a consumer media publisher, not an API provider: it did not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable API surface, and its groupnine.com domain now resolves to a third-party domain-sale landing page. This profile is retained as a VC-portfolio identity record with no scorable API artifacts.

providers.name: GurbaniNow
providers.description: Fast and Accurate Gurbani RESTful API

providers.name: Holor Media
providers.description: Holor Media was an integrated immersive media technology company founded in 2015 and based in Los Angeles and San Francisco. It focused on 360/VR content creation and distribution, building augmented and virtual reality authoring tools aimed at the next generation of social, interactive XR (extended reality) experiences, including interactive 360 apps for the Transformers film franchise. It raised seed funding from 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), Skyline Ventures, and WI Harper Group. The company is now permanently closed and its former domain (holor.com) is a parked, for-sale listing on Afternic, so there is no active developer surface, API, documentation, or SDK to profile. This record is retained as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: HopShop Inc.
providers.description: HopShop Inc. is a consumer AI fashion-discovery and creator-monetization platform, often described as "Shazam for Fashion." Shoppers upload or screenshot an outfit and HopShop's visual-search AI finds the exact item plus similar matches across 600+ brand partners, including Bloomingdale's, Nordstrom, Levi's, and Tommy Hilfiger. Creators and influencers build personalized shops, link the outfits they feature on Instagram to shoppable products, grow their communities, and earn affiliate commissions. The company is backed by 500 Global. As surfaced to the API Evangelist network, HopShop operates as a consumer-facing mobile and web application and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: iHeartMedia
providers.description: iHeartMedia is America's #1 audio company, reaching 9 out of 10 Americans every month through broadcast radio, digital streaming, podcasts, live events, and on-demand entertainment. Public API documentation, developer programs, or open API artifacts have not been identified for iHeartMedia. This repository exists to track APIs, SDKs, and developer resources should they become available.

providers.name: Invisible Universe
providers.description: Invisible Universe is a consumer entertainment company building AI-powered animated intellectual property for social platforms — described by FastCompany as "building the Pixar of the internet one TikTok at a time." It has launched multiple animated franchises reaching millions of followers and billions of views across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube, and created Invisible Studio, a proprietary AI engine that compresses short-form animated content production from weeks to hours. Backed by Initialized Capital, it operates in the consumer/media sector. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Jelli
providers.description: Jelli was a programmatic advertising technology company focused on terrestrial and broadcast radio, building a real-time platform that let advertisers buy and manage radio spots programmatically across broadcast station inventory. Backed by Battery Ventures (among other investors), Jelli was acquired by iHeartMedia in 2016 and its technology went on to power programmatic and automated audio advertising. The independent Jelli brand is now defunct - the jelli.com domain 301-redirects to tritondigital.com, and no Jelli-branded developer portal, API reference, or public API host remains. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record; the enrichment pipeline found no live Jelli developer or API surface to harvest.

providers.name: JioSaavn
providers.description: API to retrieve song information, album meta data and many more from JioSaavn

providers.name: Joyride
providers.description: Joyride was a mobile audio service that made driving more fun and more interesting, offering an in-car audio/entertainment experience for drivers and passengers. Founded by Jeff Chen (co-founder & CEO) and James Zhang (co-founder & CTO), the company raised a seed round from Cowboy Ventures and was subsequently acquired by Google, marking a successful exit. As a consumer mobile application it exposed no public developer API surface, and the product is no longer independently operated following the acquisition. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph completeness rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Jubilee Inc
providers.description: Jubilee Inc (Jubilee Media) is a Los Angeles-based digital media production company that creates discussion-based and dating video shows designed to provoke thoughtful conversation and foster human connection across social and ideological divides. Its flagship YouTube programs include Middle Ground, Odd One Out, and Ranking, alongside sister dating channels such as Love Comma Nectar (Versus 1) and the reaction and behind-the-scenes brand TwoBilee. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API or developer platform at this time, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Jumpcut
providers.description: Jumpcut (Jumpcut, Inc.) is a Y Combinator-backed, remote-first digital-media company founded in 2014 in Los Angeles that produces online courses about entrepreneurship and content creation — teaching viral YouTube growth, audience building, and launching digital products with marketing automation. It reached the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Canaan Partners. Jumpcut is a consumer education/creator business, not an API producer: it publishes no developer platform, API reference, or machine-readable API specification, so there is no API surface to onboard here. As of this profile its primary domain jumpcut.com does not resolve (registered via Namecheap through 2032 but serving no DNS/website), and customers reported losing account access in late 2025, indicating the product has wound down. Retained as an identity-only network stub.

providers.name: Kaixin001
providers.description: Kaixin001 (开心网) is a Chinese social networking website launched in March 2008 by founder Cheng Bingao, a former senior executive at Sina. It rose to mass popularity in 2009-2010 on the back of viral social games such as "Friends for Sale" and "Parking Wars" before losing ground to Renren, Sina Weibo, and WeChat. After the parent company was acquired by a listed company in 2016, the founder departed and the business pivoted toward enterprise services and internet finance, marginalizing the original social network. Kaixin001 discontinued its Flash-based social gaming on November 18, 2023, and now persists mainly as a low-activity nostalgia platform. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub of Qiming and exposes no current public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Kamcord
providers.description: Kamcord was a San Francisco-based mobile technology company (Y Combinator, Summer 2012) founded by Aditya Rathnam, Kevin Wang, and Matt Zitzmann. It offered an iOS and Android SDK that let game developers embed in-app gameplay recording, live streaming ("appcasting"), and social sharing to YouTube, Twitter, and Facebook, and grew to roughly 200 million device installs. The company later pivoted to a short-form mobile screen-content social network ("shots"). In November 2017 Lyft acquihired most of the ~15-person team, including co-founders Rathnam and Wang, and Kamcord wound down its consumer app, live streaming, and developer SDK by the end of 2017. The company is DEFUNCT and no longer operates any developer program or API. The kamcord.com domain has since been repurposed by an unrelated lifestyle/blog publisher and is NOT associated with the original Kamcord.

providers.name: Kerning Cultures
providers.description: Kerning Cultures is a Middle East and North Africa media company producing narrative journalism and audio storytelling podcasts in Arabic and English. Based in Dubai, UAE and backed by 500 Global, the Kerning Cultures Network creates original shows, branded audio, and advertising for a regional listener audience. It operates as a consumer media and content brand and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future API surface.

providers.name: KNO
providers.description: Kno, Inc. was a digital textbook and student learning platform founded in May 2009 in Santa Clara, California by CEO Osman Rashid (co-founder of Chegg) and CTO Babur Habib. Kno began as a dual-screen tablet built for students, abandoned hardware in 2011, and pivoted to eTextbook software delivered across iPad, Android, Windows and the web in partnership with textbook publishers. The company raised roughly $93 million from Andreessen Horowitz, Intel Capital, Goldman Sachs, FLOODGATE, First Round Capital, SV Angel, Advance Publications and GSV Capital before being acquired by Intel in November 2013 for approximately $15 million and rebranded as Intel Education Study, which has itself since been discontinued. As of enrichment the kno.com domain is parked and redirects to a third-party domain brokerage, and the provider exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other artifact surface to enrich.

providers.name: Kosmix
providers.description: Kosmix Corporation was a Mountain View, California topic-discovery and search company operating from roughly 2005 to 2011. Rather than returning a ranked list of links, Kosmix automatically assembled a topic "home page for the web" for any subject, aggregating and categorizing content across health, science, food, sports, politics, travel, finance and other verticals. The company also shipped the RightHealth, MeeHive and Tweetbeat properties, the last of which filtered and organized real-time Twitter activity by topic. Kosmix was acquired by Walmart in 2011 and became the nucleus of @WalmartLabs; kosmix.com later 301-redirected to walmartlabs.com and the domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical record. There is no live Kosmix developer surface, API, or documentation to enrich.

providers.name: Kuwo Music
providers.description: Kuwo Music (酷我音乐) is a Chinese online music streaming service, founded in Beijing in 2005, that grew from a desktop music player into one of China's major consumer streaming apps across desktop, web, and mobile. Kuwo merged with Kugou under China Music Corporation, which was subsequently acquired by Tencent Music Entertainment Group, and Kuwo now operates as one of TME's music apps alongside QQ Music and Kugou. Kuwo entered the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead via Qiming. It is a consumer-facing streaming property rather than an API-first provider, and no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface has been verified for it.

providers.name: Kyndoo
providers.description: Kyndoo Inc. was a San Francisco based influencer-marketing software platform that let brands find, connect to and work with social-media influencers. Its differentiator was audience authenticity: Kyndoo built a database of vetted influencers and published the "Kyndex" score, described as a credit score for influencers, which measured whether a following was made of real people with buying intent rather than purchased bot accounts. Around that database it sold campaign management, attribution and brand-safety tooling to brands, taking a service fee on the influencer deals brands negotiated through the platform. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Kyndoo was acquired by CIPIO (cipio.ai) and its web property is now offline - kyndoo.com has not served a page since early 2022. Kyndoo never published a public API, developer portal or SDK, so this profile is an identity and lifecycle record rather than an API profile.

providers.name: Locker Room *
providers.description: Locker Room was a live-audio social app for sports fans built by Betty Labs, a seed-stage startup backed by GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Precursor Ventures. Launched in October 2020, it let insiders and fans hold real-time voice conversations about sports. Betty Labs and Locker Room were acquired by Spotify in March 2021 and folded into Spotify Greenroom / Spotify Live, which Spotify has since discontinued. Locker Room no longer operates as an independent product and exposes no public developer API or portal; this profile is retained as a GV portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lowkey
providers.description: Lowkey (lowkey.gg) was a San Francisco social gaming platform that let players automatically record, review, and share their gameplay highlight clips across titles like League of Legends, VALORANT, and Among Us. Backed by Y Combinator and an a16z Series A, the company was acquired by Niantic (the developer of Pokemon GO) and the consumer product was subsequently discontinued. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no live public developer surface: the lowkey.gg domain no longer resolves/serves, and there is no public API, OpenAPI, documentation portal, SDK, or MCP server to harvest.

providers.name: Lytro
providers.description: Lytro was a light-field (plenoptic) imaging company founded in 2006 by Ren Ng and based in Mountain View, California. It shipped the first consumer light-field cameras (the Lytro and the Lytro Illum), which captured the entire light field so images could be refocused after the fact, and later pivoted to professional light-field capture for cinema and VR with Lytro Cinema and Lytro Immerge. Backed by a16z, Greylock, NEA and Qualcomm Ventures, the company wound down in March 2018 with much of its technology and talent moving to Google. It is defunct and publishes no public developer program or API; the lytro.com domain now 301-redirects to an unrelated light-field vendor (raytrix.de).

providers.name: Main Street Hub
providers.description: Main Street Hub was a marketing platform for local and small businesses, founded in Austin, Texas around 2010, that managed social media, review sites, and online customer engagement on behalf of restaurants, salons, and other Main Street merchants. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, it was acquired by GoDaddy in 2018 and folded into the GoDaddy Social product; the former mainstreethub.com domain now 301-redirects to godaddy.com/online-marketing/godaddy-social. No independent developer portal, OpenAPI, or public API surface remains, and api.mainstreethub.com does not resolve.

providers.name: Meet Cute
providers.description: Meet Cute is a New York-based media company founded in 2019 by Naomi Shah that produces and distributes original scripted romantic-comedy audio programming, releasing bite-sized 15-minute rom-com stories as podcasts across platforms such as Apple Podcasts and Spotify. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Advancit Capital, and LocalGlobe, the company was acquired by Fox Entertainment in November 2025 to serve as a rapid-development content incubator for scripted and unscripted series.
