Meet Cute is a consumer media/content brand with no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile is retained as a company record.

providers.name: mogujie
providers.description: Mogujie (蘑菇街), operated by Mogu Inc. (NYSE MOGU), is a Chinese online fashion and lifestyle social-commerce destination that pairs a shopping marketplace with live video streaming and influencer-led content across apparel, beauty, and accessories. The company was formed from the 2016 merger of Mogujie and Meilishuo, is headquartered in Hangzhou, China, and listed on the New York Stock Exchange in December 2018. Mogujie's historical third-party open platform (open.mogujie.com) has been retired and now redirects away, and no active public API developer surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: mSpot
providers.description: mSpot was a mobile cloud-based content service provider founded in 2004 by Daren Tsui (CEO) and Ed Ho (CTO) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company offered a cloud music locker that let users upload their music library and stream it from PCs, Macs, iPhone, iPad and Android devices, alongside a full-length movie rental service with content deals across Sony, Disney, Paramount, NBC/Universal, Lionsgate, Warner and others. mSpot raised roughly $2.3M in venture funding from Trinity Ventures and was acquired by Samsung Electronics in May 2012 (reported ~$8.8M) to power the Samsung Music Hub. The standalone mSpot product and brand were subsequently wound down and folded into Samsung; there is no active mSpot developer portal, API, or product surface today. This profile is retained as a historical network record.

providers.name: musical.ly
providers.description: musical.ly was a short-form lip-sync and music video social app, popular 2014-2018, that was acquired by ByteDance and merged into TikTok on 2 August 2018. The service and brand are defunct. It never published an official first-party public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI; the only known interfaces are unauthorized community reverse-engineering projects. It was surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no first-party API surface to profile.

providers.name: MySpace
providers.description: Myspace (Myspace LLC, part of the People / Entertainment Weekly Network) is a music and culture social platform focused on artist networking, music streaming, and editorial entertainment coverage. Originally one of the largest social networks of the 2000s, it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Redpoint Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Myspace operates a consumer music/entertainment website only — its former developer platform (developer.myspace.com, OpenSocial-based) has been retired and no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or API documentation surface could be found. This profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signal only, with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Myxt
providers.description: Myxt is a consumer music streaming platform operated by Paper Phones Inc., built around the tagline "Musicians. Fans. Nothing in between." Instead of forced monthly subscriptions, Myxt uses an "unlock" model that lets artists monetize audio, session files, project files, images, and videos directly, while fans support creators without a recurring commitment and can chat with the artist after each unlock. Native iOS and Android apps extend access beyond the web. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network; during enrichment no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface was found.

providers.name: Next Big Sound
providers.description: Next Big Sound was a music-industry analytics company founded in 2009 out of Techstars Boulder that tracked artists' social, streaming, and airplay signals (plays, fans, engagement across Spotify, YouTube, SoundCloud, radio and social platforms) and exposed them through a REST developer API used by labels, managers and media. It was backed by Foundry Group, Uncork Capital (SoftTech VC), Alsop Louie and IA Ventures, and was acquired by Pandora in August 2015. Its analytics became Pandora's artist tools and were folded into the Pandora / SiriusXM Artist Marketing Platform (AMP). The standalone developer API and portal (developer.nextbigsound.com) have been deprecated; nextbigsound.com now resolves to Pandora infrastructure and HTTP redirects to amp.pandora.com. This profile is retained as a network identity record for a defunct/acquired provider — no independent live API surface remains to harvest.

providers.name: Omvana
providers.description: Omvana was a meditation and personal-growth audio app developed by Mindvalley, offering guided meditations, ambient soundscapes, and mixable audio tracks for daily mindfulness practice. The standalone Omvana product has since been folded into Mindvalley; omvana.com now permanently redirects (HTTP 308) to mindvalley.com/free-meditations. No public developer, API, or partner surface is published for Omvana or the successor free-meditations offering.

providers.name: Oneforty
providers.description: Oneforty was a Twitter application marketplace and app store founded by Laura Fitton in 2009, letting users discover, review, and purchase third-party apps and services built on the Twitter API. It raised roughly $1.9M (Flybridge Capital, Javelin Venture Partners, and angels including Dave McClure) and grew to thousands of listed apps before being acquired by HubSpot in 2011. The company is defunct — the oneforty.com domain now 301-redirects to hubspot.com and exposes no developer surface, API, documentation, or SDKs. Retained in the network as a historical portfolio-lead record only.

providers.name: PerfectMarket
providers.description: Perfect Market, Inc. was a digital publishing technology company founded by Idealab in 2007 and backed by Trinity Ventures, building on the Idealab/Overture paid-search lineage. It sold software for driving traffic, engagement and advertising revenue to premium publishers, and claimed more than 200 customers including LATimes.com, ChicagoTribune.com, NBCNews.com, Mediaite.com and BusinessInsider.com. Taboola acquired Perfect Market in August 2014 for cash and stock and folded its programmatic advertising technology into the Taboola-X publisher monetization product. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no API surface: perfectmarket.com retains delegated nameservers and Google Workspace mail but resolves to no web host on the apex, www, api, developer or docs names, so there is no website, developer portal, documentation, or contract to profile.

providers.name: Periscope
providers.description: Periscope was a consumer live video streaming application (pscp.tv) that let people broadcast and watch real-time video from their mobile devices, later operated by Twitter. The service was discontinued in March 2021 and the site (https://www.pscp.tv/) now serves only a farewell notice with archived past broadcasts; it publishes no API, developer portal, or documentation. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub (backers: bessemer-venture-partners, gv, menlo-ventures) in the API Evangelist network. Enrichment confirms there is no active API surface to catalog.

providers.name: PG Studios
providers.description: PG Studios is a full-service creative media company offering animation, film production, and creative media services. The studio operates specialized divisions spanning animation production, filmmaking, audio and music composition, and game development. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, PG Studios is a creative-services business rather than an API provider: its public website markets studio capabilities and a client portfolio, and it publishes no developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal. This profile has been through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; the honest result is that there is no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: PictureWorks
providers.description: PictureWorks (PictureWorks Technology) was a digital imaging technology company based in Danville, California that built imaging tools and services for the real estate and e-commerce industries, enabling online visual presentation of products and properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. The company was acquired by Internet Pictures Corporation (IPIX) in 2000. No public developer API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or SDK surface could be located for this entity during enrichment; the active pictureworks.com (Pictureworks Group, Singapore theme-park imaging) is a separate, unrelated company and is not linked here to avoid mis-attribution.

providers.name: PoetryDB
providers.description: Enables you to get instant data from our vast poetry collection

providers.name: Pond5
providers.description: Pond5 is a royalty-free stock media marketplace where creators buy and sell video footage, music tracks, sound effects, motion graphics, images, and other digital assets. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, this profile has been through a local enrichment pass: the public web presence sits behind DataDome bot protection with no discoverable public API, developer portal, SDKs, OpenAPI, or security.txt at the time of the pass. Only live DNS/TLS/HTTP domain-security posture could be probed. Sector: media.

providers.name: Pop Up Archive
providers.description: Pop Up Archive was a startup that provided audio and podcast transcription, speech-to-text, and searchable spoken-word archiving tools, making audio content discoverable and machine-readable. It was acquired by Apple in 2017 and its independent products, developer surface, and popuparchive.com domain were retired. The domain now resolves to Apple nameservers with no active host, so there is no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API to enrich. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Bloomberg Beta and is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record; no live API surface remains.

providers.name: Pop-Up Magazine
providers.description: Pop-Up Magazine is a live magazine created for a stage, a screen, and a live audience, produced by the team behind The California Sunday Magazine. Each production combines original nonfiction storytelling, live music, illustration, animation, and photography performed on tour in theaters across the United States. The company also operates Pop-Up Magazine Brand Studio, producing custom live and multimedia storytelling for brand partners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Pop-Up Magazine is a consumer media and live-events brand; it publishes a public promotional website but exposes no developer program, public API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface, so this profile is identity- and security-posture-only.

providers.name: Pose
providers.description: Pose (pose.vn) is a Vietnamese entertainment and lifestyle media publication based in Ho Chi Minh City, covering celebrity news, beauty pageants (including Miss Universe Vietnam), fashion, beauty, health, and film and television. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a company stub. As of this enrichment pass the site is a consumer-facing content publication monetized through advertising and sponsored content, with no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Post.news
providers.description: Post.news was a social-news and microblogging platform positioned as a Twitter/X alternative, backed by a16z and founded by former Waze CEO Noam Bardin. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company has no discoverable public API surface, developer program, or documentation, and the consumer web property appears to be offline (see x-website-status). This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Prologue
providers.description: Prologue (Prologue AI) is a multimodal creative operating system that lets teams create, edit, and organize AI-generated images, video, audio, and text in a single workspace. Powered by "Prologue Intent" and a best-in-class catalog of third-party generative models, it targets professional creative workflows for agencies and brands ("crafted, not generated"). It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was discoverable — the product site is a consumer/pro web application behind bot protection.

providers.name: Quran-api
providers.description: Free Quran API Service with 90+ different languages and 400+ translations

providers.name: Radionomy (Azerion)
providers.description: Radionomy (Azerion) is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: ai-apps. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Readme typing SVG
providers.description: Customizable typing and deleting text SVG

providers.name: Recordgram
providers.description: Recordgram is a mobile music-creation platform, now operating as Cre8tor (cre8tor.app), that lets aspiring artists record songs, write lyrics, access a library of beats, and collaborate with professional producers directly from a smartphone. The company won the TechCrunch Disrupt SF 2017 Startup Battlefield and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. It is a consumer iOS/Android application with no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal surfaced at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment confirmed the consumer-app nature and the rebrand to Cre8tor.

providers.name: Renren
providers.description: Renren (人人网), originally launched as Xiaonei in 2005 and renamed in 2009, was one of China's largest social networking platforms and was widely described as the "Facebook of China," especially popular among university students. Renren Inc. listed on the NYSE in 2011; the social-networking business later declined and the assets were sold in 2018. The site is now operated by Chengdu Renren Interactive Entertainment Technology Co., Ltd. and is undergoing a service upgrade. Historically Renren ran an Open Platform with an OAuth2 REST API (wiki.dev.renren.com) for third-party login and social integration; that developer surface is now defunct and no live API endpoints respond.

providers.name: ResearchGate
providers.description: ResearchGate is a professional network and social platform for scientists and researchers, founded in 2008 in Berlin, Germany. Members use it to share and discover research publications, connect and collaborate with colleagues, ask and answer questions, and track the reach and citations of their work. The platform hosts tens of millions of researcher profiles and a large corpus of full-text papers, and is operated by ResearchGate GmbH. It exposes no publicly documented developer API surface; this profile was surfaced via the dragoneer portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Resonado Labs
providers.description: Resonado Labs is a high-velocity innovation and hardware development lab focused on improving the acoustic performance of the next generation of audio products through speaker hardware design and engineering. Backed by 500 Global, the company designs novel loudspeaker and transducer technology for consumer electronics and audio OEMs. Resonado Labs is a hardware and acoustics company; it publishes a marketing website but does not currently expose a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Rooster
providers.description: Rooster is a subscription mobile reading app built by Plympton, Inc., a literary studio co-founded by Jennifer 8. Lee, Yael Goldstein Love, and Jacky Chang. Rooster delivers serialized fiction to readers' phones in short, commute-sized installments for a flat monthly fee, drawing on Plympton's DailyLit heritage of serialized reading. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Rooster is a consumer-facing app; Plympton publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or webhook surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Schematic Labs
providers.description: Schematic Labs was a San Francisco consumer music startup founded in 2010, best known as the maker of SoundTracking, an "Instagram for songs" mobile app for sharing the music you are listening to. Backed by Google Ventures (GV), Accel Partners, and SoftBank Capital with roughly $5.9M raised, it was acquired by Rhapsody in August 2014 and wound down as a standalone company. Today soundtracking.com redirects to napster.com (Rhapsody's successor brand) and schematiclabs.com is a parked domain. No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment; this profile records the company's place in the GV portfolio graph.

providers.name: Scout.fm
providers.description: Scout.fm (Scout FM) was a podcast-curation startup whose iOS, Android, Alexa and CarPlay apps turned podcasts into personalized, radio-like stations using AI-driven recommendations across genres such as news, sports and true crime. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, Precursor Ventures, Advancit Capital and Samsung NEXT (roughly $1.4M raised), the company was acquired by Apple in September 2020 and subsequently shut down, with its apps pulled from every platform. The scout.fm domain no longer resolves and the company publishes no developer, API, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as a historical network record; there is nothing left to enrich.

providers.name: Shots Mobile
providers.description: Shots Mobile, Inc. is the company founded by John and Sam Shahidi that built the Shots selfie photo-sharing app (2013) and grew from mobile-game studio RockLive into a podcast and media business. Today shots.com presents SHOTS as a media company that helps creators turn shows into businesses through partnerships, distribution, and growth resources. It publishes a marketing/content website on WordPress.com and exposes no first-party developer or API product surface; there is no public documentation, SDK, or hosted API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Simply Measured
providers.description: Simply Measured was a Seattle-based social media analytics and reporting platform, founded in 2010 and backed by Trinity Ventures, that measured brand performance across Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and other social channels. It was acquired by Sprout Social in December 2017 and its product, brand, and developer surface were sunset and folded into Sprout Social. The simplymeasured.com domain now 301-redirects to sproutsocial.com and no independent Simply Measured API, developer portal, or documentation remains online. This record is retained as a defunct/acquired portfolio-lead marker; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Socialcam
providers.description: Socialcam was a mobile social video application (iPhone, Android, Windows Phone) for capturing, editing, and sharing short videos across social networks. Founded by Michael Seibel, Ammon Bartram, and Guillaume Luccisano out of Y Combinator (W2012) and backed by a16z, it reached roughly 16 million downloads and was acquired by Autodesk in July 2012 for $60 million. The consumer service was discontinued on October 28, 2015, and socialcam.com no longer resolves to a live web host (AWS Route 53 nameservers only, no A record), so there is no developer portal, API, documentation, or agent surface to enrich.

providers.name: Sonantic
providers.description: Sonantic was a London-based AI voice company that built hyper-realistic, emotionally expressive text-to-speech models for entertainment, gaming, and film. The company is best known for recreating Val Kilmer's voice for Top Gun: Maverick after he lost his speaking voice to throat cancer. Spotify acquired Sonantic in June 2022 for a reported 93 million euros, and the underlying TTS technology has since been folded into Spotify products, most visibly the Spotify AI DJ feature launched in 2023. As of 2026, Sonantic no longer operates as a standalone product or public API. This apis.yml entry exists as a historical and archival record of the company, its technology, and its acquisition.

providers.name: Storia Originals, Inc.
providers.description: Storia Originals, Inc. (doing business as Storiaverse) was a Los Angeles-based consumer mobile entertainment startup founded in 2023 by Agnes Kozera and David Kierzkowski. Its Storiaverse app pioneered a patent-pending "read-watch" format blending short-form reading, animation, and audio, connecting writers and animators to publish and monetize original stories across sci-fi, fantasy, horror, mystery, and comedy, including adaptations of HarperCollins titles. It raised a pre-seed round led by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; both its marketing site (storia.io) and its iOS/Android app store listings are no longer reachable (all HTTP 404), indicating the product is inactive or has been wound down.

providers.name: SumAll
providers.description: SumAll was a New York-based social media and business analytics startup, surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct - its primary domain sumall.com no longer resolves to a live product and is parked/listed for sale on Afternic. There is no live developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface to harvest, so no provider artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Sverve
providers.description: Sverve was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. During the enrichment pass the company's website (sverve.com) was offline — the origin returned HTTP 522 behind Cloudflare, and its DNS (NameBright registrar-parking MX/SPF and a "comingsoon.namebright.com" DMARC target) indicates the domain is parked and the company appears inactive. No developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or public API surface could be found, so there is nothing to enrich beyond a probed domain-security record. Left as an inactive lead.

providers.name: tempow
providers.description: Tempow was a Paris-based startup (founded 2016) building software to improve Bluetooth audio connectivity, including an operating system for true-wireless earbuds and multi-device audio streaming licensed to chipset makers and Android device manufacturers such as Motorola and TCL. Backed by Balderton Capital and C4 Ventures, Tempow was acquired by Google in 2021. The company operated as a B2B embedded-software and licensing business and never published a public developer API. Its website (www.tempow.com) no longer resolves. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment confirms there is no live API surface.

providers.name: Tennis Channel
providers.description: Tennis Channel is a United States-based cable television network and direct-to-consumer streaming service dedicated to tennis and racquet sports, including live coverage and highlights from the ATP Tour, WTA Tour, Grand Slam events, and related pickleball and padel programming. Alongside its linear TV channel it operates a subscription streaming product (Tennis Channel / formerly Tennis Channel Plus) delivering live matches, on-demand video, news, rankings, and instructional content across web, mobile, and connected-TV apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Tennis Channel publishes a consumer streaming platform but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: The Echo Nest
providers.description: The Echo Nest was a music-intelligence company, spun out of the MIT Media Lab, that ran a developer platform and API for music understanding — machine-listening audio analysis (tempo, key, energy, danceability, valence), artist and song metadata, automated playlisting and taste profiles, and the Rosetta Stone service for translating artist and track IDs across music services. It was acquired by Spotify in March 2014 (reported at roughly €49.7M / ~$100M). Spotify consolidated onto its own Web API: The Echo Nest API stopped issuing new keys on 2016-03-29 and stopped serving requests on 2016-05-31, with developers directed to the Spotify Web API (whose audio-features and audio-analysis endpoints descend from Echo Nest technology). The developer.echonest.com portal no longer resolves; the echonest.com domain now redirects to an unrelated WordPress site. This profile was surfaced as a matrix-partners portfolio company; it is retained for historical/lineage reference and has no live, public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: The Players' Tribune
providers.description: The Players' Tribune is a sports-media company that gives athletes a platform to connect directly with fans in their own words, publishing first-person stories, essays, letters, and video from professional players across football, basketball, soccer, baseball, and other sports. Founded in 2014 and backed by GV and IVP, it operates as a digital publisher rather than an API provider: an enrichment probe of theplayerstribune.com found a public sports-content website with no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface (no docs/api/developer subdomains, no /.well-known/ metadata, no llms.txt). This profile captures the company identity and the results of a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: thetab
providers.description: The Tab (thetab.com) is a UK-based digital media and entertainment publication operated by Digitalbox Publishing Ltd (Co Reg No. 09909897). It covers celebrity and reality-TV news, viral trends, gaming, politics, and university and campus culture across a network of youth-focused verticals, monetized primarily through advertising (advertise.thetab.com). Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, /.well-known/ discovery surface, or llms.txt (all probed and returned HTTP 404); this remains an editorial/advertising media property with no developer-facing product.

providers.name: Ticketfly
providers.description: Ticketfly was a San Francisco-based event-ticketing platform for independent music venues, promoters, and festivals, founded in 2008. It was acquired by Eventbrite in 2017 and, following a June 2018 data breach, was shut down in November 2018 with its music-oriented features folded into Eventbrite Music. The company is defunct: as of 2026 every Ticketfly host (www.ticketfly.com, developer.ticketfly.com) returns HTTP 301 redirects to eventbrite.com. No independent Ticketfly API, developer portal, documentation, or specification survives. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Tracksby
providers.description: Tracksby (Tracks.by) was a music marketing startup that helped artists and their managers release new music and videos through deep Facebook integration, social launch campaigns, fan email capture, and YouTube/VEVO embeds, turning each release into a fan-growth campaign. Listed on the a16z investment list, the early-2010s company is now defunct - tracks.by no longer resolves, tracksby.com is parked for sale, the @TracksBy Twitter account is gone, and its GitHub account has been inactive since 2012. No public API surface was found, so this profile records an inactive portfolio lead with no artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: TrueLens
providers.description: TrueLens was a marketing-technology startup providing social media analytics and customer intelligence. Its product, Socialgraphics, helped brands target customers using data compiled and analyzed from multiple social networks for marketing campaigns. Google Ventures (GV) led a roughly $1.2M funding round in 2012; the company was small (2-10 employees). TrueLens now appears defunct: its former domain truelens.com 301-redirects to an unrelated retailer (misterspex.de), and no public API, developer portal, or documentation could be found. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio lead; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Tumblbug
providers.description: Tumblbug (텀블벅) is a South Korean reward-based crowdfunding platform for creators, where makers launch projects and backers pledge funds to bring creative works — comics, games, publishing, design, music, film and more — to life. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Tumblbug publishes a consumer-facing web platform (help center, creator guides, pricing/advertising, terms and privacy pages) but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or open API surface; this profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Twenty-First Century Fox
providers.description: Twenty-First Century Fox was an American multinational mass media corporation that operated film, television, and cable assets before being largely acquired by The Walt Disney Company in 2019. Its remaining broadcasting and news assets continued under Fox Corporation. The company no longer exists as an independent entity and did not expose public developer APIs.

providers.name: Verome
providers.description: Music API for searching, streaming, and exploring music data from YouTube Music, YouTube, and Last.fm

providers.name: Vibely
providers.description: Vibely was a creator-community platform (surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company) that let creators host paid communities, challenges, and group chat. As of this enrichment pass the domain vibely.io no longer serves an independent product; every path — including all /.well-known/ discovery endpoints — 301-redirects to kajabi.com/features/communities, indicating Vibely was folded into Kajabi's Communities product. No standalone Vibely developer portal, API, OpenAPI, SDK, MCP server, or llms.txt could be found; the only artifact captured is a probed TLS/DNS domain-security profile of the surviving redirect domain. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired portfolio lead.

providers.name: Walkie-Talkie
providers.description: Walkie-Talkie is a Gen Z social audio platform built by Picslo Corp that hosts live audio rooms called "frequencies" — public or private channels where users tune in and talk with friends in high-fidelity audio anytime, anywhere. Thousands of public frequencies run at any given time, connecting people around topics they choose to discuss, alongside private frequencies between close friends. The company raised $3.25M in pre-seed funding from investors including Partech, Breega, Kima Ventures, Heroic Ventures, TI Platform Ventures, LDV Partners, and Diaspora Ventures. It is a consumer mobile application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Wetpaint
providers.description: Wetpaint is a media brand operating wetpaint.com, an entertainment and lifestyle publication covering Hollywood gossip, celebrity news, TV series recaps and buzz, and pop-culture storytelling. Originally a Trinity Ventures-backed wiki/collaborative-media startup, the property today runs as an ad- and affiliate-supported editorial content site with no public developer program: as of this enrichment pass it exposes no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a media-sector company record.

providers.name: Wildfire Interactive
providers.description: Wildfire Interactive, Inc. was a social media marketing software company founded in 2008 by Victoria Ransom and Alain Chuard in Redwood City, California. Its platform let brands create, optimize, and measure their presence across social networks — running branded promotions, sweepstakes, contests, and coupons plus page management, advertising, messaging, and analytics across Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest, and YouTube. Backed by the Facebook Fund, Summit Partners, Accel Partners, and Founders Fund, Wildfire was acquired by Google in 2012 and folded into Google's advertising products (DoubleClick); the standalone product was wound down by 2014. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of uncork-capital and is retained as a historical record — the company operates no independent public API surface today.

providers.name: Wonderbly *
providers.description: Wonderbly is an online publisher that makes personalized books and gifts for kids and adults. Founded in 2013 (originally as Lost My Name), it lets customers design and buy books customized with a recipient's name, themes, and occasion, and has delighted over 10 million readers worldwide. The consumer e-commerce site operates across 40+ language and regional storefronts (US, UK, AU, CA, DE, FR, NL, IT, ES). Backed by GV. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation was found during enrichment; this remains a company profile lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sinclair
providers.description: Sinclair, Inc. is a diversified media company and a leading provider of local news and sports in the United States. The company owns or operates a large portfolio of television stations and is involved in original programming, digital media, technical services, and broadcast technology innovation through subsidiaries such as Dielectric, Bitpath, ONE Media, and CAST.ERA. No public developer API or technical documentation portal is currently available.

providers.name: LifeMed Media
providers.description: LifeMed Media was a consumer health media company that operated dLife, a diabetes-focused media brand spanning dLife.com, the dLifeTV television program, the dLife Foundation, a diabetes retail store, and a section for healthcare professionals. Its editorial surface covered type 1, type 2, gestational and pre-diabetes, blood sugar management, insulin, complications, nutrition and recipes, and diabetes lifestyle content, monetized through sponsored sections from device and pharmaceutical advertisers. The company was venture backed by Battery Ventures. As of a 2026-07-19 verification pass the business appears defunct: its corporate domain lifemedmedia.com is parked for sale on HugeDomains and dlife.com no longer resolves. No developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface has ever been identified for this company.

providers.name: USA TODAY
providers.description: A major American daily national newspaper and digital news platform owned by Gannett. One of the most widely circulated newspapers in the United States covering news, sports, entertainment, and lifestyle topics.

providers.name: Wiley
providers.description: A global publishing and education company providing research, professional development, and learning solutions. Publishes peer-reviewed journals, textbooks, and digital content across science, technology, medicine, social science, and business.

providers.name: VoiceVoice
providers.description: VoiceVoice is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Radio Station Pro
providers.description: Radio Station Pro is a WordPress plugin for managing online radio stations, schedules, DJs, shows, and playlists. No public REST API has been published by the vendor at this time.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

providers.name: Slow Ventures
providers.description: Slow Ventures is a generalist early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco, with additional offices in Boston and New York. The firm leads pre-seed and seed rounds, writing typical checks of roughly $500K to $3M (averaging around $1.75M), and explicitly rejects thematic investing in favor of backing experienced founders with deep, hard-won domain expertise and genuine conviction. Slow's thesis funds rapid, high-stakes experimentation: capital that tests a novel risk or hypothesis whose validation dramatically increases a company's value and that cannot easily be funded another way. As a generalist, Slow invests across consumer and social, fintech, SaaS and enterprise/developer tools, healthcare, crypto/web3, the creator economy, and real-world operations (SMB acceleration, buyouts/rollups, franchising). The firm runs a dedicated Creator Fund backing creator-led businesses, and has deployed roughly $800M+ across multiple fund vintages since inception. Notable investments include Pinterest, Slack, Robinhood, Nextdoor, Postmates, Opendoor, Wealthfront, Casper, PillPack, Airtable, Gusto, and Solana.

providers.name: Social Capital
providers.description: Social Capital is a technology investment firm founded in 2011 by Chamath Palihapitiya (a former Facebook executive) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with co-founders Mamoon Hamid and Ted Maidenberg. Originally a traditional venture fund that stood out by backing healthcare, financial services, education, and other hard, regulated sectors the VC community had neglected, the firm pivoted in 2018 into a technology holding company that stopped accepting outside capital and now invests from its own permanent balance sheet of roughly $2.1B, aiming to "earn like Berkshire Hathaway and invest like the Red Cross." Its thesis targets multiple emerging $10T markets across deep tech commercialization, life sciences and drug discovery, the global energy transition, and creator-economy media. Chamath became known as the "SPAC King" for taking companies public through the Social Capital Hedosophia (IPOA-IPOF) vehicles, including Virgin Galactic, Opendoor, Clover Health, and SoFi. Notable investments include Slack, Box, SurveyMonkey, Wealthfront, Netskope, Intercom, Groq, Palmetto, Saildrone, and Relativity Space.

providers.name: Visioconference
providers.description: Visioconference (video conferencing) is a category of communication technology enabling real-time visual and audio communication between remote participants. This repository profiles the video conferencing API ecosystem including leading providers such as Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Webex, Digital Samba, VideoSDK, Daily.co, and others offering REST APIs for embedding and managing video conferencing functionality. The term "visioconference" is commonly used in French-speaking contexts.
